```
print(dataset_id)
```

**Kaggle credentials** must be registered in Adaption: open **[API keys settings](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings?tab=api_keys)** (sign in if prompted) and add your Kaggle API credentials there before importing.

Raw (passthrough) processing is currently supported only for local file uploads. Do not combine `processing_mode="raw"` with a Hugging Face or Kaggle URL. See [Run on non-adapted data](/autoscientist/run-on-non-adapted-data/index.md) for a local-file example.

## Upload documents

Documents are not rows yet. After the upload, Adaption counts their pages and waits for you to launch extraction, which turns the content into rows and costs credits.

Upload the file and wait for it to finish. The dataset stops at `awaiting_input` with no `row_count`:

```
dataset = client.datasets.upload_file("annual_report.pdf")
dataset_id = dataset.dataset_id

status = client.datasets.wait_for_completion(dataset_id)
print(status.status, status.row_count)
```
title: Create a dataset

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/create-a-dataset/ | Type: docs | Title: Create a dataset | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Check what extraction will cost before you launch it with [`get_preprocessing_credits`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/get_preprocessing_credits/index.md). Pages are counted in the background, so the dataset can reach `awaiting_input` before the count is done. Until then the quote is partial (`is_final` is `False`), so poll until it is final:

```
import time

quote = client.datasets.get_preprocessing_credits(dataset_id)
while not quote.is_final:
    time.sleep(2)
    quote = client.datasets.get_preprocessing_credits(dataset_id)
print(f"{quote.total_pages:.0f} pages cost {quote.extraction_cost} credits")
print(f"{quote.available_credits} credits available")
if quote.insufficient_credits:
    raise RuntimeError("Not enough credits to extract these documents")
```

Launch extraction with [`launch_preprocessing`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/launch_preprocessing/index.md), then wait again. When extraction finishes, the dataset returns to `awaiting_input`, this time with a `row_count`:

```
launch = client.datasets.launch_preprocessing(
    dataset_id,
    preprocessing_mode="per_page",
)
print(f"Reserved {launch.credits_escrowed} credits")

status = client.datasets.wait_for_completion(dataset_id)
if status.status == "failed":
    error = status.error_data
    message = (error and error.message) or "unknown error"
    raise RuntimeError(f"Document extraction failed: {message}")
print(f"Extracted {status.row_count} rows")
```

`preprocessing_mode` decides how content becomes rows: `per_document` (the default) makes one row per document, `per_page` one row per page. To extract only part of the upload, pass either `pages_to_process` or `documents_to_process`, not both. `get_preprocessing_credits` accepts the same limits, so you can quote a subset before launching it.

Launch extraction once per dataset. A second call fails with `adaption.ConflictError` (HTTP 409), and so does a launch before the upload finishes. If pages can’t be counted yet, the launch fails with HTTP 503. If the team lacks the credits, it fails with HTTP 402 and reserves nothing.

## Wait for the import

Imports run asynchronously. Poll the [dataset status](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/get_status/index.md) until ingestion has populated the dataset before starting an adaptation run:

```
import time

while True:
    status = client.datasets.get_status(dataset_id)
    if status.status == "failed":
        error = status.error_data
        message = (error and error.message) or "unknown error"
        raise RuntimeError(f"Dataset import failed: {message}")
    if status.row_count is not None:
        print(f"Imported {status.row_count} rows")
        break
    time.sleep(5)
```
title: Create a dataset

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/create-a-dataset/ | Type: docs | Title: Create a dataset | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Next, [map the imported columns](/adaptive-data/select-columns/index.md), then [configure the adaptation run](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data/index.md). For endpoint details, see the [`create`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/create/index.md) and [`get_status`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/get_status/index.md) references. The `datasets.upload_file` helper handles the create, upload, and completion steps for local files.

[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/evaluate-dataset-quality/ | Type: docs | Title: Evaluate dataset quality | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Evaluate dataset quality

> Poll evaluation status and inspect quality metrics for an adapted dataset with the Python SDK.

After an [adaptation run](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data/index.md) succeeds, evaluation compares the source and adapted data on quality dimensions measured by the platform. Evaluation runs on its own schedule, so adaptation can finish before quality results are ready.

The Python SDK exposes results in two forms:

- **[`datasets.get_evaluation(dataset_id)`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/get_evaluation/index.md)** returns evaluation status and the full `quality` result.
- **[`datasets.get(dataset_id)`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/get/index.md)** returns the dataset record and its compact `evaluation_summary`.

## Fetch evaluation results

Call `get_evaluation` with the same `dataset_id` used for the adaptation run:

```
evaluation = client.datasets.get_evaluation(dataset_id)

print(evaluation.status)
if evaluation.quality:
    print(f"Score before: {evaluation.quality.score_before}")
    print(f"Score after:  {evaluation.quality.score_after}")
    print(f"Improvement:  {evaluation.quality.improvement_percent}%")
```

When evaluation succeeds, `quality` can include before-and-after scores on a 0–10 scale, letter grades, improvement percentage, and an after-adaptation percentile. While status is `pending` or `running`, `quality` can be absent.

## Poll until evaluation finishes

Poll evaluation status with a deadline so a notebook or CI job cannot wait forever:

```
import time

deadline = time.monotonic() + 600

while True:
    evaluation = client.datasets.get_evaluation(dataset_id)
    if evaluation.status in ("succeeded", "failed", "skipped"):
        break
    if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
        raise TimeoutError("Evaluation did not finish within 10 minutes")
    time.sleep(5)

if evaluation.status == "failed":
    raise RuntimeError("Dataset evaluation failed")
if evaluation.status == "skipped":
    print("Evaluation was skipped")
elif evaluation.quality:
    print(evaluation.quality.model_dump(exclude_none=True))
```

Async clients return the same response shape with `await client.datasets.get_evaluation(dataset_id)`.

## Read the summary from the dataset

If your application already [fetches the dataset](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/get/index.md), use `evaluation_summary` for headline metrics without a separate evaluation request:

```
dataset = client.datasets.get(dataset_id)

if dataset.evaluation_summary:
    summary = dataset.evaluation_summary
    print(f"Score after: {summary.score_after}")
    print(f"Improvement: {summary.improvement_percent}%")
```

[`datasets.get_status`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/get_status/index.md) reports ingestion and adaptation progress; it does not include evaluation results.

## Complete example
title: Evaluate dataset quality

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/evaluate-dataset-quality/ | Type: docs | Title: Evaluate dataset quality | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
This script reads a completed adaptation’s dataset ID from the environment, waits for evaluation, and prints both the detailed result and compact summary:

```
import os
import time

from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()
dataset_id = os.environ["ADAPTION_DATASET_ID"]
deadline = time.monotonic() + 600

while True:
    evaluation = client.datasets.get_evaluation(dataset_id)
    print(f"Evaluation status: {evaluation.status}")

    if evaluation.status in ("succeeded", "failed", "skipped"):
        break
    if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
        raise TimeoutError("Evaluation did not finish within 10 minutes")
    time.sleep(5)

if evaluation.status == "failed":
    raise RuntimeError("Dataset evaluation failed")
if evaluation.status == "skipped":
    print("Evaluation was skipped for this dataset")
elif not evaluation.quality:
    raise RuntimeError("Evaluation succeeded without quality metrics")
else:
    print(evaluation.quality.model_dump(exclude_none=True))

dataset = client.datasets.get(dataset_id)
if dataset.evaluation_summary:
    print(dataset.evaluation_summary.model_dump(exclude_none=True))
```

Use `get_evaluation` when you need explicit pipeline status or complete quality details. Use `evaluation_summary` when a compact result on the dataset record is enough. To iterate economically on quality, [limit rows and estimate the run](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data#limit-rows-and-estimate-a-run/index.md) before scaling.
title: Evaluate dataset quality

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/expand-data/ | Type: docs | Title: Expand your data | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Expand your data

> Augment, generate similar, translate, or localize rows to increase dataset size after import or adaptation.

After you [import a dataset](/adaptive-data/create-a-dataset/index.md) and optionally [run Adaptive Data](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/adapt/index.md), you can increase row count without re-running the full adaptation pipeline. Each method below returns a **new dataset** that includes your source rows plus the added ones.

The SDK examples assume you have [configured the Python SDK](/introduction/getting-started/index.md) and set `ADAPTION_DATASET_ID` to a dataset that is ready to expand:

```
import os

from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()
dataset_id = os.environ["ADAPTION_DATASET_ID"]
```

## Data augmentation

[`datasets.augment`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/augment/index.md) retrieves additional rows from the curated pool and returns them as a new dataset. Use it when you want more examples in the same topic mix or broader coverage across topics:

- **Domain rows** match topics in your dataset.
- **General rows** come from other topics to broaden diversity.

```
estimate = client.datasets.augment(
    dataset_id,
    domain_rows=3_000,
    general_rows=1_000,
    estimate=True,
)
print(f"Estimated credits: {estimate.estimated_credits_consumed}")

response = client.datasets.augment(
    dataset_id,
    domain_rows=3_000,
    general_rows=1_000,
)
print(response.dataset_id, response.status)
```

The response carries the new dataset’s id and its current status; both are `None` for an estimate. Wait for the new dataset before you download or train on it:

```
from adaption import DatasetTimeout

try:
    final = client.datasets.wait_for_completion(response.dataset_id)
except DatasetTimeout as exc:
    print(exc.resource_id, exc.last_status)
    raise

print(final.status, final.row_count)
```

`wait_for_completion` backs off from 2 to 30 seconds and has a one-hour default timeout. A timeout stops waiting, not the expansion job. Call it again with the same dataset ID to resume tracking. The same wait applies after [similar rows](#generate-similar-rows), [`translate`](#translate-rows) and [`localize`](#localize-rows).

Omit either row parameter to skip that type of addition. Augmentation is billed on the rows retrieved. See the [`augment` reference](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/augment/index.md) for current limits and request fields.

Domain and general rows work on text datasets whose topic mix can be determined. `datasets.augment` does not support image datasets. Domain and general rows are the same curated-pool operation as `augmentation_domain_rows` and `augmentation_general_rows` on [`autoscientist.create`](/autoscientist/data-augmentation/index.md). The AutoScientist path applies those rows at training time instead of writing a new dataset.

## Generate similar rows
title: Expand your data

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/expand-data/ | Type: docs | Title: Expand your data | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Pass `similar_rows` to [`datasets.augment`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/augment/index.md) to generate new rows in the style of your dataset instead of retrieving them from the pool. Adaptive Data reads a sample of your rows, works out their topics, language, and prompt and completion conventions, and generates new rows to match. Use it when the pool has little that looks like your data, or when you want more rows that follow your own format closely:

```
estimate = client.datasets.augment(
    dataset_id,
    similar_rows=500,
    estimate=True,
)
print(f"Estimated credits: {estimate.estimated_credits_consumed}")

response = client.datasets.augment(dataset_id, similar_rows=500)
print(response.dataset_id, response.status)
```

The new dataset holds your source rows plus the generated ones.

`similar_rows` combines with `domain_rows` and `general_rows` in one call, and the new dataset holds all three kinds of row:

```
response = client.datasets.augment(
    dataset_id,
    domain_rows=3_000,
    general_rows=1_000,
    similar_rows=500,
)
```

Similar rows are billed at the same rate as pool rows, on the rows actually generated, up to `similar_rows`. A run that generates fewer rows than requested is charged only for those it delivers. Your plan may cap `similar_rows` per request; a request above the cap returns `400` with the limit in the body.

## Translate rows

[`datasets.translate`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/translate/index.md) converts a sample of existing rows into other languages. Adaptive Data supports up to 242 languages. Provide [ISO 639-1 language codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes). `sample_rate` is the fraction of source rows expanded for each target language:

```
estimate = client.datasets.translate(
    dataset_id,
    sample_rate=0.25,
    languages=["es", "fr"],
    estimate=True,
)
print(f"Estimated credits: {estimate.estimated_credits_consumed}")

response = client.datasets.translate(
    dataset_id,
    sample_rate=0.25,
    languages=["es", "fr"],
)
print(response.dataset_id, response.status)
```

With two target languages and a `0.25` sample rate, the output contains approximately `1 + (0.25 × 2) = 1.5` times as many rows as the input.

## Localize rows

[`datasets.localize`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/localize/index.md) adapts rows for both a language and a country, including locale-specific wording rather than direct translation alone. Provide country/language pairs using [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2#Officially_assigned_code_elements) and [ISO 639-1 language codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes):

```
response = client.datasets.localize(
    dataset_id,
    sample_rate=1.0,
    pairs=[
        {"country": "CA", "language": "fr"},
        {"country": "MX", "language": "es"},
    ],
)
print(response.dataset_id, response.status)
```
title: Expand your data

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/expand-data/ | Type: docs | Title: Expand your data | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Each pair creates a country- and language-specific variant rather than only translating the text.

Translate and localize are billed on output rows. Set `estimate=True` on any of these methods to price a request before it runs. Pass `idempotency_key` on any of them to make a retried request return the dataset the first request created instead of starting and charging for a second run. See the [`translate`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/translate/index.md) and [`localize`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/localize/index.md) references for the current schema and supported values.

## Match translations to their source rows

A dataset created by `translate` or `localize` holds each sampled source row alongside its variants. When you [download](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/download/index.md) it, three extra columns tell you which rows belong together:

| Column                 | Value                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target_language`      | Name of the language the row was translated or localized into: `Spanish` after `translate`, `Spanish (Mexico)` after `localize`. `original` for a source row. |
| `target_language_code` | Code for that language: `es` after `translate`, or a full locale tag such as `es-Latn-MX` after `localize`. `original` for a source row.                      |
| `translation_join_id`  | ID shared by a source row and every variant produced from it.                                                                                                 |

For example, here are four rows from the `localize` call above, in file order. Each source row shares its ID with the Spanish variant made from it:

| `original_prompt`                              | `target_language`  | `target_language_code` | `translation_join_id`                  |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| ¿Qué hacen las abejas?                         | `Spanish (Mexico)` | `es-Latn-MX`           | `847c6b29-0287-4f8a-9f6b-5b7ed555d21b` |
| What color is the sky on a clear day?          | `original`         | `original`             | `48b7feb6-0c31-4402-9078-81932756debb` |
| What do bees make?                             | `original`         | `original`             | `847c6b29-0287-4f8a-9f6b-5b7ed555d21b` |
| ¿De qué color es el cielo en un día despejado? | `Spanish (Mexico)` | `es-Latn-MX`           | `48b7feb6-0c31-4402-9078-81932756debb` |
title: Expand your data

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/expand-data/ | Type: docs | Title: Expand your data | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Rows in a group are not guaranteed to be adjacent in the file. Pivot on `translation_join_id` to put each source row next to its variants, for example to build parallel text or to keep a row and its translations in the same train or evaluation split:

```
import pandas as pd

client.datasets.download(response.dataset_id, file_format="csv").write_to_file(
    "localized.csv"
)

rows = pd.read_csv("localized.csv")

parallel = rows.pivot(
    index="translation_join_id",
    columns="target_language_code",
    values="original_prompt",
)
print(parallel)
```

The result has one row per source row and one column per language or locale, with the source text under `original`:

```
target_language_code                                                      es-Latn-MX                                         fr-Latn-CA                               original
translation_join_id
48b7feb6-0c31-4402-9078-81932756debb  ¿De qué color es el cielo en un día despejado?  De quelle couleur est le ciel par une journée ...  What color is the sky on a clear day?
847c6b29-0287-4f8a-9f6b-5b7ed555d21b                          ¿Qué hacen las abejas?            Qu'est-ce que les abeilles produisent ?                     What do bees make?
96df9709-b201-4203-913c-3a201e6d4d98                 ¿Cuántos días tiene una semana?       Combien de jours y a-t-il dans une semaine ?           How many days are in a week?
ae0e0cd4-672f-4fda-afd4-52597412ca94                 ¿Cuál es la capital de Francia?              Quelle est la capitale de la France ?         What is the capital of France?
```

`translation_join_id` carries through [`datasets.combine`](/adaptive-data/combine-datasets/index.md): rows that came from a translated or localized dataset keep their value, and rows from other sources have none.

For recipes, preference pairs, row limits, and brand controls on an adaptation run, see [Configure Adaptive Data](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data/index.md).

The methods on this page each write a new dataset and leave the source unchanged. `datasets.adapt` also accepts `translate`, `localize` and `expand`, which add rows inside its own adaptation run without creating a new dataset. See [Add rows and languages to a run](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data#add-rows-and-languages-to-a-run/index.md).
title: Expand your data

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/extend-trajectories/ | Type: docs | Title: Extend your trajectories | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Extend your trajectories

> Generate a next user turn for each conversation to build multi-turn training data that depends on earlier context.

Extend your trajectories when you want multi-turn training data that tests whether a model remembers what was said earlier in a conversation. For each row’s conversation, [`datasets.extend_trajectories`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/extend_trajectories/index.md) generates the user’s next message: a single question or request that can only be answered correctly by recalling details from earlier turns, written in the conversation’s language.

Each request creates a **new dataset** that holds the extended trajectories and leaves the source dataset unchanged. Only the next user turn is generated; no completion is generated for it.

The SDK examples assume you have [configured the Python SDK](/introduction/getting-started/index.md) and set `ADAPTION_DATASET_ID` to an [imported dataset](/adaptive-data/create-a-dataset/index.md) whose import has finished:

```
import os

from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()
dataset_id = os.environ["ADAPTION_DATASET_ID"]
```

### How it works

1. **Map the conversation.** Point `column_mapping` at a chat column, or at a prompt and completion pair. See [Map the conversation](#map-the-conversation).
2. **Estimate (optional).** Price the exact request with `estimate=True`. Nothing is created or charged.
3. **Extend.** Call `datasets.extend_trajectories` to create the new dataset and start the run.
4. **Wait and download.** Wait for the new dataset, then [download the rows](#download-the-extended-dataset).

## Map the conversation

The trajectory is the conversation up to and including the assistant’s final reply, and the new user turn is generated after that reply. A row whose conversation has no user turn, or does not end on a non-empty assistant reply, is skipped and left out of the new dataset. Provide the trajectory with **one** of two mappings:

| Mapping                 | Use when                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `chat`                  | One column holds each row’s whole conversation as a list of turns, ending on the assistant’s reply. Send `chat` alone.                             |
| `prompt` + `completion` | `prompt` holds the conversation up to and including the user’s last turn. `completion` holds the assistant’s final reply as plain text. Send both. |

A list of turns is an array of `{"role": ..., "content": ...}` objects, such as a column of arrays in JSONL or Parquet, or a JSON string encoding that array. `prompt` also accepts a plain string, read as a single user turn, so a single-turn prompt and completion dataset works as is:
title: Extend your trajectories

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/extend-trajectories/ | Type: docs | Title: Extend your trajectories | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
```
{"prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": "I'm planning a trip to Kyoto in April."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "April is cherry blossom season..."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Which temples should I visit?"}], "response": "Kiyomizu-dera and Fushimi Inari..."}
{"prompt": "What's a good first houseplant?", "response": "A pothos is hard to kill..."}
```

For a chat dataset:

```
response = client.datasets.extend_trajectories(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={"chat": "messages"},
)
```

For a prompt and completion dataset:

```
response = client.datasets.extend_trajectories(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={"prompt": "prompt", "completion": "response"},
)
```

`chat` cannot be combined with `prompt` or `completion`, and `prompt` and `completion` must be sent together. `context`, `universal_prompt`, and `image` mappings are not currently supported; a request that includes them is rejected rather than run without them.

## Extend the trajectories

Set `estimate=True` to validate the mapping and price the request before it runs:

```
estimate = client.datasets.extend_trajectories(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={"chat": "messages"},
    estimate=True,
)
print(f"Estimated credits: {estimate.estimated_credits_consumed}")
print(f"Estimated minutes: {estimate.estimated_minutes}")
```

Then start the run. Use `job_specification` to cap the number of rows processed or to make retries safe. Row counts are subject to your plan’s per-launch row limit:

```
from uuid import uuid4

response = client.datasets.extend_trajectories(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={"chat": "messages"},
    job_specification={
        "max_rows": 1_000,
        "idempotency_key": str(uuid4()),
    },
)
print(response.dataset_id, response.run_id)
```

The response carries the new dataset’s `dataset_id` and the `run_id` of its run; both are `None` for an estimate. Use the new `dataset_id`, not the source dataset’s, for status and download:

```
from adaption import DatasetTimeout

try:
    final = client.datasets.wait_for_completion(response.dataset_id)
except DatasetTimeout as exc:
    print(exc.resource_id, exc.last_status)
    raise

print(final.status, final.row_count)
```

`wait_for_completion` backs off from 2 to 30 seconds and has a one-hour default timeout. A timeout stops waiting, not the run. Call it again with the same dataset ID to resume tracking.

The new dataset can have fewer rows than the source. Rows that are [skipped](#map-the-conversation) or can’t be extended are left out of it.

Credits are billed as for an [Adaptive Data run](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/adapt/index.md). Keep the same `idempotency_key` if you retry the request. A retry with that key returns the `dataset_id` and `run_id` the first request created, with zero estimates, instead of starting and charging for a second run.

## Extend an adapted dataset
title: Extend your trajectories

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/extend-trajectories/ | Type: docs | Title: Extend your trajectories | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
If the dataset has finished an [Adaptive Data run](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/adapt/index.md), the extension builds on its adapted dataset instead of the original uploaded file. `column_mapping` then names columns of the adapted dataset, so you can extend the adapted replies with `enhanced_completion`:

```
response = client.datasets.extend_trajectories(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={
        "prompt": "prompt",
        "completion": "enhanced_completion",
    },
)
```

Map the original completion column instead, such as `response`, to extend the replies as they were uploaded.

Only the `prompt` + `completion` mapping applies to an adapted dataset. Adaptation splits a chat column into `original_prompt` and `original_completion`, so map `original_prompt` as `prompt` instead of sending `chat`.

## Download the extended dataset

When you [download](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/download/index.md) the new dataset, each row carries its conversation plus an `extended_prompt` column holding the generated next user turn. The conversation columns follow the same naming as an adaptation run’s download:

| Mapping                 | Conversation columns                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `chat`                  | `original_prompt` holds the conversation up to the user’s last turn, and `original_completion` the final reply. |
| `prompt` + `completion` | Your own column names, such as `prompt` and `response`.                                                         |

An extension of an adapted dataset also keeps the adapted columns, such as `enhanced_completion`, next to `extended_prompt`.

```
client.datasets.download(response.dataset_id, file_format="jsonl").write_to_file(
    "extended.jsonl"
)
```

See the [`extend_trajectories` reference](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/extend_trajectories/index.md) for the current request and response fields.

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/invent-a-dataset/ | Type: docs | Title: Invent a dataset | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Invent a dataset

> Generate a model-ready dataset from scratch, with no source dataset required.

Invent generates a model-ready dataset from scratch—no source dataset required. Describe your dataset with a prompt, optionally narrow with domains and subdomains, and the API creates a dataset for your task.

Use [`datasets.create`](/adaptive-data/create-a-dataset/index.md) instead when you want to import and adapt an existing dataset.

### What you can build

- **Instruction datasets** pair prompts with generated completions for supervised fine-tuning.
- **Preference pairs** rank two completions against each other for preference-based training.

### How it works

1. **Describe your dataset.** Use the `dataset_prompt` and optional `domains` and `subdomains` to guide the dataset invention process.
2. **Estimate (optional).** Price the exact request with `estimate=True`. Nothing is created or charged.
3. **Generate.** Call [`datasets.invent`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/invent/index.md) to create the dataset and start generation. The call returns immediately with status `running`.
4. **Poll and download.** Poll [`datasets.get`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/get/index.md) until the status is `succeeded`, then [download the rows](#download-the-rows).

## Generate a dataset

A single call to `datasets.invent` creates the dataset and starts generating rows from your description and optional domain selections. The examples assume you have [installed the Python SDK and set `ADAPTION_API_KEY`](/introduction/getting-started/index.md).

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

dataset = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    rows=1000,
    name="Clinical Q&A",
)

dataset_id = dataset.id
print(dataset_id, dataset.status)  # running
```

### Describe the dataset

To invent a dataset, provide **at least one** of the following parameters:

| Parameter        | Notes                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dataset_prompt` | Description of the data to generate. If omitted, a description is generated from your domain selections. Maximum 10,000 characters. |
| `domains`        | Domain codes to generate from. See [Choose domains and subdomains](#choose-domains-and-subdomains).                                 |
| `subdomains`     | Qualified subdomain codes that narrow generation. See [Choose domains and subdomains](#choose-domains-and-subdomains).              |

### Request parameters
title: Invent a dataset

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/invent-a-dataset/ | Type: docs | Title: Invent a dataset | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
| Parameter         | Required | Notes                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rows`            | Yes      | Number of rows to generate. Subject to your plan’s per-launch row limit.                                                                                 |
| `name`            | No       | Display name for the invented dataset.                                                                                                                   |
| `training_type`   | No       | `instruction_dataset` (default) or `preference_pairs`. See [Choose the output format](#choose-the-output-format).                                        |
| `translate`       | No       | Translates a sample of the generated rows into other languages. See [Expand across languages and locales](#expand-across-languages-and-locales).         |
| `localize`        | No       | Localizes a sample of the generated rows to country and language pairs. See [Expand across languages and locales](#expand-across-languages-and-locales). |
| `estimate`        | No       | Returns a credit estimate without creating or launching a dataset. Defaults to `False`.                                                                  |
| `idempotency_key` | No       | Makes retries safe. Repeating a request with the same key returns the original dataset instead of starting generation again. Maximum 255 characters.     |

### Price a request first

Set `estimate=True` to price the exact request. Nothing is generated or charged:

```
estimate = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    domains=["medical"],
    subdomains=[
        "medical.symptoms_diagnosis",
        "medical.preventive_care",
    ],
    rows=1000,
    estimate=True,
)

print(f"Estimated credits: {estimate.estimated_credits}")
print(f"Available credits: {estimate.available_credits}")
```

## Choose domains and subdomains

Fetch the current codes accepted by `datasets.invent` rather than hardcoding them:

```
response = client.datasets.invent_domains()

for domain in response.domains:
    print(domain.code, domain.title)
    for subdomain in domain.subdomains:
        print("  ", subdomain.code, subdomain.title)
```

### Domain and subdomain fields
title: Invent a dataset

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/invent-a-dataset/ | Type: docs | Title: Invent a dataset | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
| Field        | Description                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`       | The value to send in `domains` or `subdomains`. Domain codes are values such as `medical`; subdomain codes are qualified values such as `medical.symptoms_diagnosis`. |
| `title`      | Human-readable name for the domain or subdomain.                                                                                                                      |
| `subdomains` | Subdomains available within a domain. An empty list means the domain has no subdomains.                                                                               |

### Narrow with subdomains

Pass subdomain codes exactly as returned by `invent_domains`. `subdomains` is a flat list of qualified codes:

Here, the medical portion is narrowed to the selected subdomains. The legal portion draws from the full legal domain because no legal subdomains were provided.

```
dataset = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    domains=["medical", "legal"],
    subdomains=[
        "medical.symptoms_diagnosis",
        "medical.preventive_care",
    ],
    rows=1000,
)
```

### Combine multiple domains

Every code in `domains` contributes to the same generation run. For a domain without subdivisions, pass its domain code and omit subdomains for it.

## Configure generation

Configure the output format, expand languages, and make retries safe.

### Choose the output format

`training_type` defaults to `instruction_dataset`. Set it to `preference_pairs` for chosen and rejected completion pairs:

```
dataset = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    domains=["medical"],
    rows=1000,
    training_type="preference_pairs",
)
```

Use `instruction_dataset` for standard supervised fine-tuning. Use `preference_pairs` for preference-based training such as DPO. The same formats are described in [Configure Adaptive Data](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data#generate-preference-pairs/index.md).

### Expand across languages and locales

`translate` and `localize` add rows in other languages, the same way as [translating and localizing an existing dataset](/adaptive-data/expand-data#translate-rows/index.md):
title: Invent a dataset

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/invent-a-dataset/ | Type: docs | Title: Invent a dataset | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
- `translate` adds a translated variant of each sampled row for every target language.
- `localize` adds a variant for every country and language pair, using locale-specific wording rather than direct translation alone.

Pass either one, or both in the same request. Each takes its own `sample_rate`: the fraction of invented rows expanded for each target, between `0.01` and `1`. Credits are billed on the expanded output row count.

```
dataset = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    domains=["medical"],
    rows=1000,
    translate={
        "languages": ["es", "fr"],
        "sample_rate": 0.25,
    },
    localize={
        "pairs": [{"country": "ES", "language": "ca"}],
        "sample_rate": 0.1,
    },
)
```

This request delivers and bills about `1,000 × (1 + 0.25 × 2 + 0.1 × 1) = 1,600` rows.

Unsupported language codes and country/language pairs return a `400` response before anything is created.

`language_expansion` is deprecated. It holds one mode at a time and cannot be combined with `translate` or `localize`. Requests that already use it keep working.

### Make retries safe

Provide an idempotency key when a network failure might cause your application to retry the request:

```
dataset = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    domains=["medical"],
    rows=1000,
    idempotency_key="clinical-qa-2026-09-02",
)
```

Repeating the same request with this key returns the original dataset instead of starting another generation run.

### Put it together

```
domains = ["medical"]
subdomains = ["medical.symptoms_diagnosis"]

estimate = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    domains=domains,
    subdomains=subdomains,
    rows=1000,
    estimate=True,
)
print(f"Estimated credits: {estimate.estimated_credits}")

dataset = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    name="Clinical Q&A",
    domains=domains,
    subdomains=subdomains,
    rows=1000,
    training_type="instruction_dataset",
    idempotency_key="clinical-qa-2026-09-02",
)
dataset_id = dataset.id
print(dataset_id, dataset.status)  # running
```

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/invent-a-dataset/ | Type: docs | Title: Invent a dataset | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
## Check status and download

Poll `datasets.get` with the invented dataset ID until generation reports `succeeded` or `failed`.

### Poll until generation finishes

```
import time

while True:
    record = client.datasets.get(dataset_id)
    if record.status == "succeeded":
        break
    if record.status == "failed":
        error = record.error_data
        message = (error and error.message) or "unknown error"
        raise RuntimeError(f"Dataset generation failed: {message}")
    time.sleep(5)

print(f"Generated {record.row_count} rows")
```

### Download the rows

Download the completed dataset as JSON Lines, JSON, CSV, or Parquet:

```
client.datasets.download(
    dataset_id,
    file_format="jsonl",
).write_to_file("clinical-qa.jsonl")
```

See [`datasets.download`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/download/index.md) for all response and streaming options.

### Complete example

```
import time

from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

domains = ["medical"]
subdomains = ["medical.symptoms_diagnosis"]

estimate = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    domains=domains,
    subdomains=subdomains,
    rows=1000,
    estimate=True,
)
print(f"Estimated credits: {estimate.estimated_credits}")

dataset = client.datasets.invent(
    dataset_prompt=(
        "A dataset of medical question-answer pairs covering diagnoses, treatments, "
        "drug explanations, and healthcare roles. Each entry includes a prompt and a "
        "detailed, expert-generated response."
    ),
    name="Clinical Q&A",
    domains=domains,
    subdomains=subdomains,
    rows=1000,
    training_type="instruction_dataset",
    idempotency_key="clinical-qa-2026-09-02",
)
dataset_id = dataset.id
print(dataset_id, dataset.status)  # running

assert dataset_id is not None

while True:
    record = client.datasets.get(dataset_id)
    if record.status == "succeeded":
        break
    if record.status == "failed":
        error = record.error_data
        message = (error and error.message) or "unknown error"
        raise RuntimeError(f"Dataset generation failed: {message}")
    time.sleep(5)

print(f"Generated {record.row_count} rows")

client.datasets.download(
    dataset_id,
    file_format="jsonl",
).write_to_file("clinical-qa.jsonl")
```

To train on the generated dataset, pass its ID to [`autoscientist.create`](/autoscientist/running-autoscientist/index.md):

```
run = client.autoscientist.create(dataset_id=dataset_id)
print(run.id, run.status)
```

[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/overview/ | Type: docs | Title: Overview | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Overview

> Understand what Adaptive Data produces and how data moves from import through adaptation and evaluation.

Adaptive Data analyzes the structure of your source data, then adapts and optimizes it into a model-ready dataset for AI training.

## What you can build

- **Instruction datasets** — prompts paired with expected completions for supervised fine-tuning
- **Preference pairs** — two completions compared to indicate which is better, for preference-based training

## How it works

Adaptive Data runs through six stages:

1. **[Import](/adaptive-data/create-a-dataset/index.md)** — bring in data from a local file, Hugging Face, or Kaggle.
2. **[Map columns](/adaptive-data/select-columns/index.md)** — identify prompt, completion, context, image, or chat data.
3. **[Apply recipes](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data#apply-recipes/index.md)** — optionally deduplicate or rephrase prompts and generate reasoning traces.
4. **[Expand](/adaptive-data/expand-data/index.md)** — optionally augment, translate, or localize rows into a new dataset.
5. **[Set brand controls](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data#configure-brand-controls/index.md)** — optionally control length, safety, grounding, tone, and other Blueprint instructions.
6. **[Adapt](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/adapt/index.md) and [evaluate](/adaptive-data/evaluate-dataset-quality/index.md)** — start adaptation, then compare quality signals for the source and adapted data.

To build multi-turn data, you can [extend your trajectories](/adaptive-data/extend-trajectories/index.md) with a generated next user turn for each conversation. After completing multiple runs, you can [combine their datasets](/adaptive-data/combine-datasets/index.md) into one new training dataset.

## Supported inputs

- **File formats**: CSV, JSON, JSONL, Parquet, PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, ZIP, and TXT
- **Hugging Face**: point at a dataset URL
- **Kaggle**: point at a dataset page URL

Start with the [Adaptive Data quickstart](/adaptive-data-quickstart/index.md), or browse the complete [API reference](/api/python/index.md).

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/select-columns/ | Type: docs | Title: Select columns to adapt | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Select columns to adapt

> Map dataset columns to prompt, completion, context, image, or chat roles before running Adaptive Data.

A dataset is made of rows and named columns. Adaptive Data needs to know which column contains the instruction, which contains the answer, and which columns provide supporting material. In the Python SDK, you define these roles with **`column_mapping`** on [`datasets.adapt`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/adapt/index.md).

Column mapping is the foundation for later steps such as [recipes and brand controls](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data/index.md), [evaluation](/adaptive-data/evaluate-dataset-quality/index.md), and [export](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/download/index.md).

## Map a prompt or completion

Every run needs at least one of these anchors:

- **Prompt** — the question, instruction, or task to complete.
- **Completion** — the expected response or answer.

You only need one. If the other is missing, Adaptive Data can generate it.

The examples below assume you have [installed and configured the Python SDK](/introduction/getting-started/index.md) and [uploaded a dataset](/adaptive-data/create-a-dataset/index.md) to obtain `dataset_id`.

### Prompt without a completion

If the dataset contains prompts but no completions, map only the prompt column. Adaptive Data generates a completion for each row.

For example, a CSV with an `instruction` column might contain real tasks such as “Explain why leaves appear green” and “Convert 15 miles to kilometres”:

```
run = client.datasets.adapt(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={"prompt": "instruction"},
)
```

### Completion without a prompt

If the dataset contains high-quality answers but no prompts, map only the completion column. Adaptive Data synthesizes an appropriate prompt for each answer.

For example, a CSV with a `response` column might contain reference answers such as “Leaves appear green because chlorophyll reflects green wavelengths of light”:

```
run = client.datasets.adapt(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={"completion": "response"},
)
```

### Prompt and completion

Most instruction datasets already contain both roles:

```
run = client.datasets.adapt(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={
        "prompt": "instruction",
        "completion": "response",
    },
)
```

## Add context columns

Context columns hold per-row background information, reference data, or metadata that the model needs to answer the prompt. Unlike `prompt` and `completion`, **`context` is a list**, so you can map multiple columns.

This example maps a document question-answering dataset with a title and passage for each question:

```
run = client.datasets.adapt(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={
        "prompt": "question",
        "completion": "answer",
        "context": ["document_title", "document_body"],
    },
)
```

Common patterns include:
title: Select columns to adapt

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/select-columns/ | Type: docs | Title: Select columns to adapt | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
- **Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)** — map the query as `prompt`, retrieved passages as `context`, and the reference answer as `completion`.
- **Per-row metadata** — provide an audience, tone, locale, or product line alongside each prompt.
- **Universal prompt with context** — apply one instruction to every row while context columns provide the row-specific material.

For one instruction shared by every row, use a universal prompt. For visual context, see [Map an image column](#map-an-image-column).

## Use a universal prompt

If every row should use the same instruction and the dataset does not have a prompt column, define a **universal prompt**. Context or image columns then supply the per-row content on which that instruction operates.

In the Python SDK, set `universal_prompt` directly in `column_mapping`. This example classifies reviews while using the existing `sentiment` column as the expected completion:

```
run = client.datasets.adapt(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={
        "universal_prompt": (
            "Classify the sentiment of this review as positive, neutral, "
            "or negative. Respond with one word."
        ),
        "context": ["review"],
        "completion": "sentiment",
    },
)
```

You can configure the same mapping in the web app:

### 1. Select “I don’t have prompt”

On the columns step, locate the **Prompt column** card and select **I don’t have prompt**.

![The columns step of the wizard with the Prompt column card and its "I don't have prompt" checkbox highlighted, alongside the Context column and Completion column cards.](/universal-prompts/dont-have-prompt.png)

The prompt card displays two choices:

- **Let adaption create prompt** generates a prompt for each completion.
- **Write universal prompt** applies one instruction to every row.

### 2. Write the shared instruction

Select **Write universal prompt**, then enter the instruction in **Enter prompt for all entries…**.

![The expanded prompt card highlighting the "Write universal prompt" link and a textarea with placeholder "Enter prompt for all entries..." underneath, with the "Let adaption create prompt" toggle visible above.](/universal-prompts/universal-prompt.png)

Write a complete, self-contained instruction that identifies the task and expected output. For example:

> Classify the sentiment of this review as positive, neutral, or negative. Respond with one word.

The same `universal_prompt` value is available through the [`datasets.adapt` API](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/adapt/index.md) and Python SDK, so app and programmatic runs can use the same mapping.

## Map an image column

Images use the dedicated **`image`** mapping rather than the `context` list. The following mapping uses the public [MathVision dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/MathLLMs/MathVision): `question` contains the prompt, `decoded_image` contains the figure, and `answer` contains the expected answer.
title: Select columns to adapt

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/adaptive-data/select-columns/ | Type: docs | Title: Select columns to adapt | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
```
run = client.datasets.adapt(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={
        "prompt": "question",
        "completion": "answer",
        "image": "decoded_image",
    },
)
```

![Mapping the MathVision columns in the column selection step of the adaptation wizard: question as the prompt, decoded\_image as image context, and answer as the completion.](/multimodal-context/column-selection.png)

Use image columns for visual question answering, captioning, classification, OCR, and other multimodal tasks.

### Supported image inputs

Supported representations depend on the dataset source.

#### Hugging Face

- **`bytes`** — raw image bytes
- **`hf_struct`** — a Hugging Face `Image()` feature
- **`list`** — an array of image bytes
- **`url`** — an absolute `http(s)` URL
- **`path`** — a relative path, such as an `imagefolder` entry

#### Kaggle

- Image folders without a manifest, such as `train/<class>/*.png`
- A CSV or Parquet manifest with an image column
- A tabular file with a bytes or URL column

#### Direct file upload

For directly uploaded CSV, Parquet, JSON, JSONL, XLSX, and similar files:

- **`bytes`**, **`hf_struct`**, or **`list`**
- **`url`** — an absolute `http(s)` URL

## Map a chat column

![Map a chat column](/chat-column.png)

A chat column contains a multi-turn conversation in the same shape used by OpenAI-style chat APIs. Each cell is a JSON array of turns:

```
[
  { "role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant." },
  { "role": "user", "content": "How do I reset my password?" },
  {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": "Open Settings, select Account, then select Reset password."
  }
]
```

Map the column containing those arrays:

```
run = client.datasets.adapt(
    dataset_id,
    column_mapping={"chat": "messages"},
)
```

A `chat` mapping is mutually exclusive with `prompt`, `completion`, and `context` mappings.

When you map `chat`, Adaptive Data derives the prompt and completion from the conversation. Use `chat` for existing multi-turn data; use `prompt` and `completion` for single instruction-and-answer pairs.

## Plain text and chat-turn arrays

Cells mapped as `prompt` or `completion` can contain either:

- **Plain text** — a string in each cell.
- **Chat-turn arrays** — a JSON array of `{"role": "...", "content": "..."}` objects.

For example, a structured completion can preserve an exchange within one cell:

```
[
  { "role": "user", "content": "Summarize this email." },
  {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": "The customer accepted the revised delivery date."
  }
]
```

Adaptive Data parses valid arrays into chat turns and treats other values as plain text. For a full multi-turn conversation stored in one column, prefer the purpose-built `chat` mapping.

See **ColumnMapping** on the [`datasets.adapt` reference](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/adapt/index.md) for the current schema.
title: Select columns to adapt

[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/api/resources/autoscientist/ | Type: docs | Title: Autoscientist | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Autoscientist

## Create an AutoScientist run

**post** `/api/v1/autoscientist`

Starts an iterative AutoScientist loop on a dataset you own. The loop runs up to max_iterations training cycles, stopping early when target_win_rate is achieved. Omitted parameters are resolved to platform defaults for the selected model and returned in the response. Poll GET /autoscientist/{experiment_id} for status, then GET /autoscientist/{experiment_id}/download once it succeeds. The dataset must have finished processing: adapt it first with [POST /datasets/{dataset_id}/adapt](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/adapt), or ingest it raw with [POST /datasets](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/create) when it already holds prompt and completion columns.

### Body Parameters

- `dataset_id: string`

  The dataset to train on. Must be a dataset you own that has finished processing.

- `model: optional string`

  Base model id from GET /autoscientist/models. By default, AutoScientist selects a suitable model. The resolved model is returned in the response `model` field.

- `training_method: optional "instruction" or "alignment"`

  Training objective. Pass `alignment` to train on preference pairs; the dataset must have been prepared with `training_type: preference_pairs`. An alignment run trains in two stages — supervised first, then preference — and this run reports the first until the second begins. Supplying `alignment` for any other dataset has no effect: there are no rejected responses to train against, so the run stays `instruction`. Omitted, it defaults to `instruction` unless an alignment run was already configured for this dataset in the dashboard.

  - `"instruction"`

  - `"alignment"`

- `data_format: optional "chat" or "instruction"`

  Encoding used for the training rows handed to the training provider. Applies to raw datasets only — for an adapted dataset the platform resolves the encoding and this value is ignored. Defaults to `chat`.

  - `"chat"`

  - `"instruction"`

- `column_mapping: optional object { prompt, completion, reasoning_trace, 2 more }`

  Which dataset columns feed training. When omitted, AutoScientist infers the mapping from the dataset. Required columns depend on the data format.

  - `prompt: optional string`

    Source column holding the prompt/instruction text.

  - `completion: optional string`

    Source column holding the target completion/response. Used for supervised (sft) training.

  - `reasoning_trace: optional string`

    Optional source column holding a reasoning trace to train on. Supported on instruction runs with a model whose GET /autoscientist/models entry reports `train_with_reasoning: true`; naming it with any other model on such a run is rejected.

  - `chosen: optional string`

## Recommend hyperparameters

**post** `/api/v1/autoscientist/recommend-hyperparams`

Returns the hyperparameters AutoScientist derives for a model and the dataset's effective training size (rows plus planned augmentation). Nothing is launched. Omit `model` to size against the model POST /autoscientist would select for this dataset; the resolved id is returned with the values. POST /autoscientist applies the same values when `hyperparams` is omitted.

### Body Parameters

- `dataset_id: string`

  The dataset the hyperparameters are sized for. Must be a dataset you own that has finished processing.

- `model: optional string`

  Base model id from GET /autoscientist/models to tune for. Omit to size the recommendation against the model POST /autoscientist selects for this dataset; the resolved id is returned in the response `model` field. That pick assumes no `column_mapping`, so a create request supplying `column_mapping.reasoning_trace` can resolve a different model. Pass the returned `model` back on create to pin it.

- `augmentation_domain_rows: optional number`

  Number of synthetic domain-targeted rows you plan to generate. These are additional to your own rows and count toward the effective training size, so the recommendation matches what you will launch. Defaults to 0 (no augmentation).

- `augmentation_general_rows: optional number`

  Number of synthetic general-diversity rows you plan to generate. These are additional to your own rows and count toward the effective training size. Defaults to 0 (no augmentation).

### Returns

- `model: string`

  Resolved base model id the recommendation is sized for: the value you sent, or the automatically selected model when `model` was omitted. Pass it back as `model` on POST /autoscientist to launch against the same model.

- `hyperparams: object { training_type, n_epochs, learning_rate, 16 more }`

# Datasets

## Create a dataset from file upload, HuggingFace, Kaggle, Google Sheets, or a public S3 or Cloud Storage object

**post** `/api/v1/datasets`

Unified ingest endpoint. Pass source.url to start an async import — the provider is inferred from the URL host (HuggingFace, Kaggle, Google Sheets, or one public S3 or Cloud Storage object ending in .csv, .json, .jsonl, or .parquet). Omit it to get upload instructions for a presigned S3 PUT. Adapt the result with [POST /datasets/{dataset_id}/adapt](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/adapt), or send it straight to training with [POST /autoscientist](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create) when it already holds prompt and completion columns.

### Body Parameters

- `source: object { url, files, sheet_names, 6 more }`

  Dataset source. Pass `url` to import from HuggingFace, Kaggle, Google Sheets, or a public S3 or Cloud Storage object (.csv, .json, .jsonl, or .parquet), or `name` + `file_format` to upload a file. For Sheets, optional `sheet_names` selects tabs (omit or `[]` for all).

  - `url: optional string`

    HuggingFace, Kaggle, Google Sheets, or public S3 or Cloud Storage object URL. Provide it to import from that source; omit it to upload a local file instead. An object URL is one https file ending in .csv, .json, .jsonl, or .parquet.

  - `files: optional array of string`

    File paths to download from the source. Required with HuggingFace/Kaggle `url`. Not used for Google Sheets — use `sheet_names` (or `sheet_name`) instead — or for a public S3 or Cloud Storage object URL.

  - `sheet_names: optional array of string`

    Google Sheets tab titles to import. Only for Google Sheets `url`. Omit or pass `[]` to import every tab; pass one or more titles to import only those tabs.

  - `sheet_name: optional string`

    Legacy single Google Sheets tab title. Ignored when `sheet_names` is present (including `[]`).

  - `access: optional "oauth" or "public"`

    Google Sheets only. `public` imports a link-shared spreadsheet without a connected Google account. `oauth` (default) uses the connected account and may be unavailable on some accounts.

    - `"oauth"`

    - `"public"`

  - `name: optional string`

    Name for the dataset. Required for file uploads, where it may double as a filename ("sales-data.csv") to supply the format; derived from the URL for provider imports.

  - `file_format: optional "csv" or "json" or "jsonl" or 8 more`

    Format of the file being uploaded. Optional when `name` ends in a supported extension — it is inferred from there, and an explicit value overrides it.

    - `"csv"`

    - `"json"`

    - `"jsonl"`

    - `"parquet"`

    - `"pdf"`

    - `"docx"`

    - `"pptx"`

    - `"xlsx"`

    - `"html"`

    - `"zip"`

    - `"txt"`

  - `processing_mode: optional "adapt" or "raw"`
title: Datasets

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/api/resources/datasets/ | Type: docs | Title: Datasets | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
How the data is ingested, for both uploads and provider imports. `adapt` (default) runs it through the adaptation pipeline. `raw` materializes the data straight to a trainable dataset with no augmentation, and needs a column_mapping plus tabular input — `file_format` for an upload, or `files` for an import. Imported files are read as one dataset, so they must share a single format and schema. Either can then be fine-tuned or run through AutoScientist.

    - `"adapt"`

    - `"raw"`

  - `column_mapping: optional object { prompt, completion, chosen, 3 more }`

    Required when processing_mode is `raw`: which columns to canonicalize as the prompt and the answer — either a completion, or a chosen / rejected pair. Ignored when the dataset is adapted.

    - `prompt: string`

      Name of the raw column holding the prompt / input text

    - `completion: optional string`

      Name of the raw column holding the completion / target text. Required unless chosen and rejected are given.

    - `chosen: optional string`

      Name of the raw column holding the preferred response. Give it together with rejected to ingest a preference dataset.

    - `rejected: optional string`

      Name of the raw column holding the dispreferred response. Give it together with chosen.

    - `reasoning_trace: optional string`

      Name of the raw column holding a reasoning trace. It is stored as `original_reasoning_trace`, kept apart from the `reasoning_trace` an adaptation generates; name that column as `column_mapping.reasoning_trace` when you launch training to train on it.

    - `context: optional array of string`

      Names of raw columns to fold in as context alongside the prompt. Each is validated against the uploaded file at ingestion; an unknown name fails the request listing the available columns. The columns themselves are kept in the dataset as well as folded.

### Returns

- `dataset_id: string`

  ID of the newly created dataset

- `status: string`

  Current dataset status

- `upload_instructions: optional object { url, method, s3_key }`

  Upload instructions for file sources. PUT your file to the provided URL.

  - `url: string`

    Pre-signed URL for uploading the file

  - `method: string`

    HTTP method to use

  - `s3_key: string`

    S3 object key — pass this back in the complete request if needed for verification

### Example

```http
curl https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/datasets \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADAPTION_API_KEY" \
    -d '{
          "source": {}
        }'
```

#### Response

```json
{
  "dataset_id": "dataset_id",
  "status": "status",
  "upload_instructions": {
    "url": "https://s3.amazonaws.com/bucket/key?X-Amz-Signature=...",

}
```

## Download the processed dataset

**get** `/api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/download`

Streams the processed rows in the requested file format. Works on datasets with status `ready` (full output) and also on datasets with status `failed` — in the failed case the stream contains only the rows that were successfully processed before the run aborted, which is useful for recovering partial output from interrupted jobs. Returns 422 only when no run has ever started on this dataset.

**Image columns (JSON / JSONL):** Rows may include `original_image` only when the mapped image column is also in `configured_column_mapping.context`. Read `image_column_formats` from `GET /datasets/{dataset_id}` and look up the active image column to determine encoding: `embedded_bytes` → `{ bytes, path: null }` with base64 bytes; `url` or `file_reference` → presigned HTTPS URL string. When images are not surfaced, `original_image` is omitted and internal `s3://` URIs are never returned. See schema `ProcessedDatasetExportOriginalImageFieldDto`. In CSV and Parquet, embedded bytes appear as a JSON string in the cell.

**Response body:** binary in every format. `fileFormat=parquet` returns a gzipped tar archive of one or more Parquet shards (`.tar.gz`), not a single `.parquet` file — extract it before reading. CSV, JSON and JSONL bodies are UTF-8 text and can be decoded directly.

### Path Parameters

- `dataset_id: string`

### Query Parameters

- `fileFormat: optional "csv" or "json" or "jsonl" or "parquet"`

  Output file format. Defaults to `csv` if omitted.

  - `"csv"`

  - `"json"`

  - `"jsonl"`

  - `"parquet"`

### Example

```http
curl https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/download \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADAPTION_API_KEY"
```

Translate a sample of the rows into further languages, adding one row per sampled row and language. Combines with `localize`; output row count ≈ input × (1 + translate.sample_rate × languages + localize.sample_rate × pairs), and credits are billed on output rows.

  Passing `translate`, `localize` or `expand` sets the whole selection for this run: a mode the request leaves out is turned off, including one saved in the dashboard. With none of them (and no `language_expansion`), the selection saved on the dataset is used. Cannot be combined with `language_expansion`.

  - `languages: array of string`

    Target languages, as ISO 639-1 codes. Each sampled row gains one translated row per language. Unsupported codes are rejected with a sample of the supported ones.

  - `sample_rate: number`

    Fraction of rows translated into each language. At 0.25 with two languages, 1,000 rows become 1,500.

- `localize: optional object { pairs, sample_rate }`

  Localize a sample of the rows to country/language pairs, adding one row per sampled row and pair. Combines with `translate` and `expand`, with the same rules: passing any of them sets the whole selection for this run. Cannot be combined with `language_expansion`.

  - `pairs: array of object { country, language }`

    Target country/language pairs. Each sampled row gains one row localized to each pair — translated into the language and adapted to that country’s conventions. Unsupported combinations are rejected.

    - `country: string`

      ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

    - `language: string`

      Language code, as ISO 639-1 — optionally with a script subtag. Supported pairs include codes that are not two letters (`zh-Hant` for Taiwan, `yue` for Hong Kong), so the length is not pinned at two here. Membership is decided against the supported-pair list, which names an unsupported entry in its own 400.

  - `sample_rate: number`

    Fraction of rows localized to each pair. At 0.25 with one pair, 1,000 rows become 1,250.

- `expand: optional object { similar_rows, domain_rows, general_rows }`

  Add rows before adaptation: generated in the style of this dataset, or retrieved from matching and other topics. They are adapted along with the dataset’s own rows into this dataset, so its row count grows by their total. Translation and localization apply to the dataset’s own rows only.

  Each block costs 1 credit per 100 rows, rounded up, on top of the adaptation; the estimate includes it. Set at least one count above 0. Returns 400, leaving the saved selection unchanged, when Expand is not enabled for the organization or the dataset has image context; a column mapping with no chat, prompt or completion column or universal prompt to seed from is a 400 too. Combines with `translate` and `localize`, with the same rules: passing any of them sets the whole selection for this run. Cannot be combined with `language_expansion`.

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/api/resources/datasets/ | Type: docs | Title: Datasets | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
New rows to generate in the style of this dataset. A sample of its rows is analysed for topic, language and prompt/completion conventions, and new rows are generated to match. Defaults to 0.

    Rows to retrieve from topics matching this dataset. Defaults to 0.

    Rows to retrieve from other topics, to broaden the dataset. Defaults to 0.

- `language_expansion: optional object { type, languages, pairs, sample_rate }`

  Deprecated: use `translate` and `localize`, which can be combined. Holds one mode, translate or localize.

  Three-state field:

  - **omitted** — leaves any prior expansion config on the dataset unchanged (no-op). A wizard-saved expansion is preserved across SDK-driven /adapt calls that pass neither `language_expansion` nor `translate` / `localize`.
  - **`language_expansion: null`** — explicitly clears any prior expansion config on this dataset (overrides wizard state), including a dashboard-selected Expand.

    Target language codes (required when type=translate, forbidden when type=localize). Mostly ISO 639-1 two-letter codes such as `es`, with three-letter codes where no two-letter code exists (`fil`, `yue`) and script-tagged codes for Chinese (`zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant`). Matching is case-insensitive, and bare `zh` resolves to `zh-Hans`. Validated against the supported language list at request time; unknown values return 400 with a sample of supported codes.

    Country/language pairs (required when type=localize, forbidden when type=translate). Each pair is validated against the supported country/language pair list at request time.

      ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

      Language code, as ISO 639-1 — optionally with a script subtag. Membership is decided against the supported-pair list, which names an unsupported entry in its own 400.

    Fraction (0.01–1) of input rows that are expanded per target. Output rows ≈ input × (1 + sample_rate × target_count). Required. Credits are billed on the expanded output row count.

  How to adapt the dataset. `instruction_dataset` (default) produces enhanced prompt/completion pairs for SFT; `preference_pairs` generates chosen/rejected pairs for DPO. Source columns are the same in both cases — `column_mapping.prompt` (and optionally `completion`) — the chosen/rejected fields are produced by the adaptation pipeline.

  - `"preference_pairs"`

- `estimate: optional boolean`

  When true, validates the request and returns the estimated credit cost without starting a run. The request’s `column_mapping` and expansion fields are still saved to the dataset, as they are what the estimate prices.

- `translate: optional object { languages, sample_rate }`

  Translate a sample of the rows into further languages, adding one row per sampled row and language. Combines with `localize`; output row count ≈ input × (1 + translate.sample_rate × languages + localize.sample_rate × pairs), and credits are billed on output rows.

With none of them (and no `language_expansion`), the selection saved on the dataset is used. Cannot be combined with `language_expansion`.

- `localize: optional object { pairs, sample_rate }`

  Localize a sample of the rows to country/language pairs, adding one row per sampled row and pair. Combines with `translate` and `expand`, with the same rules: passing any of them sets the whole selection for this run. Cannot be combined with `language_expansion`.

  - `pairs: array of object { country, language }`

    Target country/language pairs. Each sampled row gains one row localized to each pair — translated into the language and adapted to that country’s conventions. Unsupported combinations are rejected.

    - `country: string`

      ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

    - `language: string`

      Language code, as ISO 639-1 — optionally with a script subtag. Supported pairs include codes that are not two letters (`zh-Hant` for Taiwan, `yue` for Hong Kong), so the length is not pinned at two here. Membership is decided against the supported-pair list, which names an unsupported entry in its own 400.

## Extend trajectories with a next user turn (or estimate cost)

**post** `/api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/extend-trajectories`
title: Datasets

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/api/resources/datasets/ | Type: docs | Title: Datasets | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
For each row's conversation, generates the user's next message: a single question or request that can only be answered correctly by remembering details from earlier in the conversation, written in the conversation's language. No completion is generated for it. Each request creates a new dataset for the result, returned as `dataset_id`; the dataset in the path is left unchanged. Poll GET /datasets/{dataset_id}/status and download from GET /datasets/{dataset_id}/download with the new id. If the dataset has been adapted (POST /datasets/{dataset_id}/adapt finished), the extension builds on its adapted download: `column_mapping` names columns of that download, so `column_mapping.completion` can be `enhanced_completion`, and the result keeps the adapted columns next to `extended_prompt`. Only `prompt` + `completion` applies there, since adapt splits a chat column into `original_prompt` and `original_completion`. Otherwise the extension reads the uploaded file, with one of two mappings. `column_mapping.chat`: a column of `{"role", "content"}` turns (or a JSON string of that list), ending on the assistant's reply. Or `column_mapping.prompt` with `column_mapping.completion`: the conversation up to the user's last turn (a turn list, or a plain string), plus the final reply as plain text. Each row of the result carries the conversation (split as for /adapt) plus an `extended_prompt` column. `context`, `universal_prompt` and `image` mappings are not currently supported. Credits and status polling behave as for /adapt; an `idempotency_key` replays the extension it first created, returning its `dataset_id` and `run_id` with zero estimates, since the replay starts and charges nothing (as for /translate). Set estimate=true to validate and get a cost quote without starting a run.

### Path Parameters

- `dataset_id: string`

### Body Parameters

- `column_mapping: optional object { chat, prompt, completion }`

  Column role assignments. Required for real runs, optional for estimate-only requests.

  - `chat: optional string`

    Column holding each row's conversation as a list of `{"role", "content"}` turns (or a JSON string encoding that list), ending on the assistant's reply. The full conversation is the trajectory the next user message is generated from. Send `chat` alone, or `prompt` with `completion` instead. Not available on an adapted dataset: adapt splits the chat column into `original_prompt` and `original_completion`, so map those with `prompt` and `completion`.

  - `prompt: optional string`

    Column holding the conversation up to and including the user's last turn: a list of `{"role", "content"}` turns (or a JSON string encoding that list), or a plain string read as a single user turn. Requires `completion`; not allowed with `chat`. On an adapted dataset, a column of its download: `original_prompt` if it was adapted from a chat column, otherwise the dataset's own prompt column.

  - `completion: optional string`
title: Datasets

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/api/resources/datasets/ | Type: docs | Title: Datasets | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
