## Generate a dataset from scratch

**post** `/api/v1/datasets/invent`

Creates a dataset and starts generating it. Describe the data either by taxonomy — `domains` and/or `subdomains` — or in your own words with `dataset_prompt`: when neither taxonomy field is given, the domains and subdomains are inferred from the prompt. Explicit taxonomy is authoritative and disables that inference. If the prompt cannot be mapped onto the catalog (or inference is unavailable), the request is rejected with `400` asking for explicit `domains`/`subdomains` — it is never widened to every domain. Returns immediately — poll `GET /datasets/{id}` for the status and `GET /datasets/{id}/download` once it reports `succeeded`. Set `estimate: true` to price a request without generating anything.

### Body Parameters

- `name: optional string`

  Display name for the invented dataset.

- `training_type: optional "instruction_dataset" or "preference_pairs"`

  Shape of the generated data — the same field and values as `datasets.adapt`. `instruction_dataset` produces prompt/completion rows; `preference_pairs` produces ranked completion pairs. Note this is the shape of the DATA, not the training method (elsewhere `training_type` means LoRA vs full fine-tuning). Defaults to `instruction_dataset`. The download carries the generated text in `enhanced_prompt` / `enhanced_completion`; `original_*` are null, since invented data has no source rows it was derived from.

  - `"instruction_dataset"`

  - `"preference_pairs"`

- `domains: optional array of string`

  Domain codes to generate from, e.g. `medical`. Optional: omit it and the domains come from the parents of your `subdomains`, or — when `subdomains` is omitted too — are inferred from `dataset_prompt`. When you do supply it, it is authoritative: inference is skipped, and a subdomain naming a domain that is not listed here is rejected rather than silently added. Retrieve the valid codes from `GET /datasets/invent/domains`.

- `subdomains: optional array of string`
title: Datasets

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/api/resources/datasets/ | Type: docs | Title: Datasets | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Narrow generation to specific subdomains, as `domain.subdomain` codes e.g. `medical.symptoms_diagnosis`. Qualified by their domain because a bare code can belong to more than one (`wildlife` sits under both agriculture and animal nature). Requested domains with no subdomain listed here are generated across all of theirs. Optional: with neither this nor `domains`, the taxonomy is inferred from `dataset_prompt`. Supplying it disables that inference. Retrieve the valid codes from `GET /datasets/invent/domains`.

- `rows: number`

  Number of rows to generate, subject to your plan’s per-launch row cap. Treat it as a target: the delivered count can land slightly either side of it, so read `row_count` on the finished dataset for what was actually produced.

- `translate: optional object { languages, sample_rate }`

  Translate a sample of the generated rows into further languages, adding one row per sampled row and language. Combines with `localize`. Credits are billed on the POST-expansion row count, so setting this quotes and charges above `rows`. Cannot be combined with `language_expansion`.

  - `languages: array of string`

    Target languages, as ISO 639-1 codes. Each sampled row gains one translated row per language. Unsupported codes are rejected with a sample of the supported ones.

  - `sample_rate: number`

    Fraction of rows translated into each language. At 0.25 with two languages, 1,000 rows become 1,500.

- `localize: optional object { pairs, sample_rate }`

  Localize a sample of the generated rows to country/language pairs, adding one row per sampled row and pair. Combines with `translate`. Credits are billed on the POST-expansion row count. Cannot be combined with `language_expansion`.

  - `pairs: array of object { country, language }`

    Target country/language pairs. Each sampled row gains one row localized to each pair — translated into the language and adapted to that country’s conventions. Unsupported combinations are rejected.

    - `country: string`

      ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

    - `language: string`

      Language code, as ISO 639-1 — optionally with a script subtag. Supported pairs include codes that are not two letters (`zh-Hant` for Taiwan, `yue` for Hong Kong), so the length is not pinned at two here. Membership is decided against the supported-pair list, which names an unsupported entry in its own 400.

  - `sample_rate: number`

    Fraction of rows localized to each pair. At 0.25 with one pair, 1,000 rows become 1,250.

- `language_expansion: optional object { type, languages, pairs, sample_rate }`

  Deprecated: use `translate` and `localize`, which can be combined. Optionally translate or localize the generated rows into further languages. Credits are billed on the POST-expansion row count, so setting this quotes and charges above `rows`. `sample_rate` (0-1) is the share of rows expanded.

  - `type: "translate" or "localize"`
title: Datasets

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/api/resources/datasets/ | Type: docs | Title: Datasets | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Expansion mode. `translate` produces one new row variant per target language; `localize` produces one new row variant per country/language pair.

    - `"translate"`

    - `"localize"`

  - `languages: optional array of string`

    Target language codes (required when type=translate, forbidden when type=localize). Mostly ISO 639-1 two-letter codes such as `es`, with three-letter codes where no two-letter code exists (`fil`, `yue`) and script-tagged codes for Chinese (`zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant`). Matching is case-insensitive, and bare `zh` resolves to `zh-Hans`. Validated against the supported language list at request time; unknown values return 400 with a sample of supported codes.

  - `pairs: optional array of object { country, language }`

    Country/language pairs (required when type=localize, forbidden when type=translate). Each pair is validated against the supported country/language pair list at request time.

    - `country: string`

      ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

    - `language: string`

      Language code, as ISO 639-1 — optionally with a script subtag. Supported pairs include codes that are not two letters (`zh-Hant` for Taiwan, `yue` for Hong Kong), so the length is not pinned at two here. Membership is decided against the supported-pair list, which names an unsupported entry in its own 400.

  - `sample_rate: number`

    Fraction (0.01–1) of input rows that are expanded per target. Output rows ≈ input × (1 + sample_rate × target_count). Required. Credits are billed on the expanded output row count.

- `dataset_prompt: optional string`

  Free-text description of the data you want, in your own words — the wizard shows this as "Dataset Details". Drives the semantic search that selects rows, so a specific prompt yields more relevant data, and it is woven into the generation instructions. Written for you from your domain selections when omitted. When `domains` and `subdomains` are both omitted this is required, and the domains and subdomains are inferred from it; if none can be inferred the request is rejected with `400` asking for explicit `domains`/`subdomains` rather than generating across every domain.

- `prompt: optional string`

  Deprecated alias for `dataset_prompt`, kept for existing clients. Use `dataset_prompt` in new code. `prompt` will be removed in a future release.

- `estimate: optional boolean`

  Price the request without creating or charging anything. Mirrors `datasets.adapt` — the response carries the same fields either way, with the dataset fields null when this is set.

- `idempotency_key: optional string`

  Client-supplied key making retries safe. Repeating a request with the same key returns the original dataset instead of generating again.

### Returns

- `estimate: boolean`

  True when this response priced the request without running it.

- `id: string`

  Dataset id, or null on an estimate. Pass it straight to `finetune_jobs.create` or `autoscientist.create` once the status is `succeeded`.

## Launch document preprocessing

**post** `/api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/launch-preprocessing`

Extracts the text, tables and figures of an uploaded document dataset (pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx, html, or a zip of them) into rows. After the upload completes, such a dataset reports `awaiting_input` until this is called. Reserves credits from the page count of the selected documents — quote them first with GET /datasets/{dataset_id}/preprocessing-credits — then starts extraction. Poll GET /datasets/{dataset_id}/status: it reports `pending` while extracting and `awaiting_input` once the rows are ready, at which point call POST /datasets/{dataset_id}/adapt.

### Path Parameters

- `dataset_id: string`

### Body Parameters

- `pages_to_process: optional number`

  Maximum number of pages to process. Documents are included until this budget is reached. If omitted, all pages are processed.

- `documents_to_process: optional number`

  Maximum number of documents to process. If omitted, all documents are processed.

- `preprocessing_mode: optional "per_document" or "per_page"`

  How extracted content becomes rows: `per_document` (default) makes one row per document, `per_page` one row per page. Omit to keep the mode already set on the dataset.

  - `"per_document"`

  - `"per_page"`

### Returns

- `dataset_id: string`

  ID of the dataset

- `status: string`

  Dataset status after the launch. Poll GET /datasets/{dataset_id}/status until it reports `awaiting_input`, then call POST /datasets/{dataset_id}/adapt.

- `credits_escrowed: optional number`

  Credits reserved for extracting the selected documents

- `pages_to_process: optional number`

  Total pages across the documents selected for extraction

- `documents_selected: optional number`

  Number of documents selected for extraction

- `documents_total: optional number`

  Number of documents in the dataset

### Example

```http
curl https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/launch-preprocessing \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADAPTION_API_KEY" \
    -d '{
          "preprocessing_mode": "per_document"
        }'
```

#### Response

```json
{
  "dataset_id": "dataset_id",
  "status": "pending",
  "credits_escrowed": 0,
  "pages_to_process": 0,
  "documents_selected": 0,
  "documents_total": 0
}
```

**post** `/api/v1/datasets/upload/initiate-batch`

Initiate a batch upload. A batch must be homogeneous: either all document formats (pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx, html, zip) or all tabular formats (csv, json, jsonl, parquet). Mixed batches are rejected. Mixing the two is rejected because the two pipelines use different credit models and preprocessing stages. TXT files are permissive: they may be included in either kind of batch (or alone, producing a tabular dataset). complete-batch converts TXT contents to csv/jsonl and merges them into the resulting dataset.

## Validate that a set of Datasets can be combined

**post** `/api/v1/datasets/combine/validate`

Synchronous compatibility check. Returns a single `issues` array containing both blockers (`level: "error"`) and reconcilable concerns (`level: "warning"`). `compatible: false` means at least one error-level issue is present (cardinality, ownership, status, run_id). Warning-level entries — column-type mismatches, DPO sources missing ranked generations — are non-blocking; the merge resolves them automatically (mixed types downgrade to instruction_dataset, type mismatches CAST to a common type, etc.). Nothing is written.

### Body Parameters

- `dataset_ids: array of string`

  Source Dataset IDs to combine. Must all belong to the caller’s org and be in a combinable state.

### Returns

- `compatible: boolean`

  Whether the proposed merge can proceed.

- `training_type: optional "instruction_dataset" or "preference_pairs"`

  Resolved training type for a compatible merge. Homogeneous source sets inherit their shared type; mixed instruction + preference sets resolve to `instruction_dataset`.

  - `"instruction_dataset"`

  - `"preference_pairs"`

- `total_estimated_rows: optional number`

  Sum of processed_rows across all sources for a compatible merge.

- `issues: array of object { code, level, message, 9 more }`

  Validation diagnostics. Errors block the merge; warnings describe reconciliation the merge performs automatically.

  - `code: "too_few_sources" or "too_many_sources" or "duplicate_source_ids" or 10 more`

    Stable machine-readable validation issue code.

    - `"too_few_sources"`

    - `"too_many_sources"`

    - `"duplicate_source_ids"`

    - `"sources_too_large"`

    - `"dataset_not_found"`

## Generate a model response

**post** `/api/v1/responses`

Creates a Responses API response through the inference gateway.

### Header Parameters

- `"X-Organization-Id": optional string`

- `traceparent: optional string`

### Body Parameters

- `model: string`

  Hosted model identifier, or `stack:<slug>` to call one of your inference stacks. A stack supplies its model and default tools; explicitly requested MCP tools must be enabled on the stack, while file_search can name any of the caller's authorized adapted datasets.

- `input: optional string or array of object { role, content }  or map[unknown]`

  Text input, or an ordered array of messages and items replayed from earlier responses. May be omitted when previous_response_id supplies stored conversation history.

  - `string`

  - `array of object { role, content }  or map[unknown]`

    - `ResponseInputMessageDto object { role, content }`

      - `role: "user" or "assistant" or "system" or "developer"`

        - `"user"`

        - `"assistant"`

        - `"system"`

        - `"developer"`

      - `content: string or array of map[unknown]`

        Text, or an array of content parts: input_text, input_image (image_url as an https or base64 data URL), or input_file (file_url, or filename with base64 file_data). Which parts a model accepts depends on the model; one that cannot read a part returns 400. input_file.file_id is not supported.

        - `string`

        - `array of map[unknown]`

    - `map[unknown]`

      An item replayed from an earlier response: message, reasoning, mcp_list_tools, mcp_call, mcp_approval_request, or mcp_approval_response.

- `instructions: optional string`

  System-level instructions for the model.

- `agentic_memory: optional boolean`

  Use agentic memory for this request: relevant memories from earlier turns with this stack are added to the model instructions, and the turn may be used to build new memories. Omitted or null uses the stack's agentic memory setting; requests that do not name a stack default to false.

- `self_improvement: optional boolean`

  Enable self-improvement for this request. Omitted or null uses the stack's setting. Only stack models accept true.

- `max_output_tokens: optional number`

  Maximum number of tokens the model may generate.

- `temperature: optional number`

  Sampling temperature.

- `stream: optional boolean`

  Whether to stream semantic response events using server-sent events.

- `tools: optional array of object { type, server_label, authorization, 4 more }  or object { type, dataset_ids, search_mode }  or object { type, filters, search_context_size, user_location }  or 2 more`

Responses API tools. Catalog MCP entries are hosted by Adaption; MCP entries with server_url are called by Adaption with caller-owned authorization; file_search runs over authorized adapted datasets; web_search searches the public web; code_execution runs in an owner-scoped, network-blocked sandbox. With `model: stack:<id>`, omitted tools means the stack's configured tools (none when tool_choice is "none"), and an empty array means no tools; requested hosted MCP labels must be enabled on the stack, and file_search uses the stack dataset scope when dataset_ids is omitted. connector_id MCP tools are not supported.

  - `McpRequestToolDto object { type, server_label, authorization, 4 more }`

    - `type: "mcp"`

      - `"mcp"`

    - `server_label: string`

      Label used to identify this MCP server in tool calls. For hosted tools, use a catalog id from GET /tools.

    - `authorization: optional string`

      Authorization for this request. For server_url tools, this exact value is forwarded as the Authorization header. For hosted tools, it is the connector credential used instead of the stored connection. Never stored, logged or echoed back.

    - `server_url: optional string`

      Caller-provided public HTTPS MCP endpoint. Adaption calls it directly.

    - `server_description: optional string`

      Description of a caller-provided remote MCP server.

    - `allowed_tools: optional array of string or object { tool_names, read_only }`

      Narrow the connector's tools: an array of tool names, or { tool_names?, read_only? }. Every name must be a tool the connector exposes.

      - `array of string`

      - `object { tool_names, read_only }`

        - `tool_names: optional array of string`

        - `read_only: optional boolean`

    - `require_approval: optional "always" or "never" or object { always, never }`

      Which calls wait for your approval: 'always', 'never', or { always?, never? } tool filters. Unset uses the saved tool permission, which defaults to allow without approval. A call that needs approval ends the response with an `mcp_approval_request` item; replay the output with an `mcp_approval_response` input item to continue.

      - `"always" or "never"`

        - `"never"`

# Tools

## List host-side tools

**get** `/api/v1/tools`

Lists the tools the orchestrator can run inside a turn, each annotated with whether this caller can use it. Tools the caller cannot use are returned with a reason rather than hidden.

### Returns

- `object: "list"`

  - `"list"`

- `data: array of object { server_label, type, name, 10 more }`

  - `server_label: string`

    The `server_label` to reference this connector by in a request, e.g. `{ "type": "mcp", "server_label": "slack" }`.

  - `type: "mcp"`

    Responses API tool type to send in the `tools` array.

    - `"mcp"`

  - `name: string`

  - `description: string`

  - `auth: "none" or "platform" or "caller" or "connection"`

    Where the outbound credential comes from. `connection` tools use a connection you authorise once, or an `authorization` passed on the request; `caller` tools always take it from the request.

    - `"none"`

    - `"platform"`

    - `"caller"`

    - `"connection"`

  - `connect: "oauth" or "secret"`

    How a `connection` tool is connected: `oauth` through the browser flow at `connect_path`, `secret` by storing one with POST /connections. Null for tools that use no stored connection.

    - `"oauth"`

    - `"secret"`

  - `connect_path: string`

    For an `oauth` tool, the GET path (under the API prefix) that starts its browser connect flow — usually /oauth/{server_label}/connect; Google Drive uses /oauth/google/connect, the shared "Connect Google". Null for tools not connected through OAuth.

  - `logo_url: string`

    URL of the connector's logo, for showing it in a UI. Null for tools without one.

  - `mode: "hosted_proxy" or "remote_mcp"`

    How the tool connects. `hosted_proxy`: we run the MCP server against the provider API. `remote_mcp`: we connect as a client to the vendor-hosted MCP server.

    - `"hosted_proxy"`

    - `"remote_mcp"`

  - `default_require_approval: "always" or "never"`

    Approval posture applied when the request's tool entry does not set `require_approval`. Defaults to `never`; callers may require approval for all tools or specific write tools.

    - `"always"`

    - `"never"`

  - `required_scope: string`

    Scope a scoped API key must hold to use this tool.

  - `available: boolean`

    Whether this caller can use the tool right now.

  - `unavailable_reason: optional "not_implemented" or "disabled" or "requires_plan" or "requires_scope"`

    Why the tool is unavailable. Returned rather than omitting the tool, so a caller can tell "not on your plan" from "does not exist".

    - `"not_implemented"`

    - `"disabled"`

    - `"requires_plan"`

    - `"requires_scope"`

### Example

```http
curl https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/tools \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADAPTION_API_KEY"
```

#### Response

# Training Models

## List available base models for training (deprecated)

**get** `/api/v1/training-models`

Deprecated alias of `GET /autoscientist/models`, kept for existing clients. Returns the set of base models that can be used as the `model` field when creating a training job. Use `GET /autoscientist/models` in new code.

### Returns

- `models: array of object { id, display_name, model_size, 4 more }`

  - `id: string`

    Identifier to pass as `model` when creating a job.

  - `display_name: string`

    Human-readable model name.

  - `model_size: optional string`

    Parameter count label (e.g. "8B", "70B").

  - `context_length: optional number`

    Maximum context window in tokens.

  - `methods: array of string`

    Training methods supported (e.g. ["sft", "dpo"]).

  - `training_types: array of string`

    Training types supported (e.g. ["lora", "full"]).

  - `train_with_reasoning: boolean`

    Whether this model trains on reasoning traces. When false, mapping a `column_mapping.reasoning_trace` on this model is rejected rather than trained without the trace.

### Example

```http
curl https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/training-models \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADAPTION_API_KEY"
```

#### Response

```json
{
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "id",
      "display_name": "display_name",
      "model_size": "model_size",
      "context_length": 0,
      "methods": [
        "string"
      ],
      "training_types": [
        "string"
      ],
      "train_with_reasoning": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Domain Types

### Training Model List Response

- `TrainingModelListResponse object { models }`

  - `models: array of object { id, display_name, model_size, 4 more }`

    - `id: string`

      Identifier to pass as `model` when creating a job.

    - `display_name: string`

      Human-readable model name.

    - `model_size: optional string`

      Parameter count label (e.g. "8B", "70B").

    - `context_length: optional number`

      Maximum context window in tokens.

    - `methods: array of string`

      Training methods supported (e.g. ["sft", "dpo"]).

    - `training_types: array of string`

      Training types supported (e.g. ["lora", "full"]).

    - `train_with_reasoning: boolean`

      Whether this model trains on reasoning traces. When false, mapping a `column_mapping.reasoning_trace` on this model is rejected rather than trained without the trace.

[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist-quickstart/ | Type: docs | Title: AutoScientist quickstart | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# AutoScientist quickstart

> Create a training-ready dataset, run AutoScientist, and download the best model checkpoint.

**Try it in Google Colab**

Follow the [AutoScientist API Colab notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/16Zly8_sDqQSP86MvdgTJ1I1T6Vjq6bkJ?usp=sharing) for an interactive walkthrough.

This guide requires `adaption >= 0.7.0`. It uses [raw processing](/autoscientist/run-on-non-adapted-data/index.md) for a short, standalone example. For best results, first improve your dataset with [Adaptive Data](/adaptive-data-quickstart/index.md), then pass that adapted dataset’s ID to AutoScientist. See the [AutoScientist overview](/autoscientist/overview/index.md) for how the research loop works and how to interpret its results.

## Install the SDK

Terminal window

```
pip install "adaption>=0.7.0"
```

## Create an API key

1. [Sign in](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/auth) to Adaption.

2. Open [**Settings**](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings), then open [**API keys**](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings?tab=api_keys).

3. Create a key and copy it. You will not be able to view the key again.

Store API keys in environment variables or a secret manager. Do not commit them to source control.

## Use the key in Python

For local testing, you can pass the key directly:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption(api_key="pt_live_...")
```

For applications and CI, set `ADAPTION_API_KEY`:

Terminal window

```
export ADAPTION_API_KEY="pt_live_..."
```

The SDK reads the environment variable automatically:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()
```

## Create a training-ready dataset

[Raw dataset creation](/autoscientist/run-on-non-adapted-data/index.md) is appropriate only when a local file already contains prompt and completion columns. This example uses `training_data.csv` with `instruction` and `response` columns:

```
dataset = client.datasets.upload_file(
    "training_data.csv",
    processing_mode="raw",
    column_mapping={
        "prompt": "instruction",
        "completion": "response",
    },
)
dataset_id = dataset.dataset_id
print(dataset_id)
```

The upload is processed asynchronously after it is completed. Poll the [dataset status](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/get_status/index.md) until the row count is available before using the dataset:

```
import time

while True:
    status = client.datasets.get_status(dataset_id)
    if status.status == "failed":
        err = status.error_data
        msg = (err and err.message) or "unknown error"
        raise RuntimeError(f"Ingestion failed: {msg}")
    if status.row_count is not None:
        print(f"Imported {status.row_count} rows")
        break
    time.sleep(5)
```

## Augment the dataset with additional rows
title: AutoScientist quickstart

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist-quickstart/ | Type: docs | Title: AutoScientist quickstart | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
[Augmentation](/autoscientist/data-augmentation/index.md) is optional but strongly recommended. Many of our models require a minimum dataset size to guarantee reasonable performance. See [supported models](/autoscientist/supported-models/index.md) for specific requirements.

This example targets at least 20,000 domain rows, then adds enough general-purpose rows for them to make up 40% of the augmented dataset.

**Why add general-purpose rows?** Fine-tuning on domain-specific data alone can cause **catastrophic forgetting**; the model loses general capabilities it learned during pre-training. Mixing in general-purpose data preserves these existing strengths while the model learns your domain, leading to a more robust and well-rounded fine-tune.

```
import math

dataset = client.datasets.get(dataset_id=dataset_id)

domain_rows_to_add = max(0, 20_000 - (dataset.row_count or 0))
total_domain_rows = (dataset.row_count or 0) + domain_rows_to_add

target_general_ratio = 0.4
general_rows_to_add = math.ceil(
    target_general_ratio
    * total_domain_rows
    / (1 - target_general_ratio)
)

print(f"Domain rows to add: {domain_rows_to_add}")
print(f"General rows to add: {general_rows_to_add}")
```

## Run AutoScientist

Create an [AutoScientist run](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create/index.md) from the prepared dataset:

```
run = client.autoscientist.create(
    dataset_id=dataset_id,
    augmentation_domain_rows=domain_rows_to_add,
    augmentation_general_rows=general_rows_to_add,
)
print(run.id, run.status)  # "pending"
```

To specify a model for your run, pass the `model` parameter to `client.autoscientist.create()`. If omitted, AutoScientist automatically selects the best model for your dataset. For comprehensive details on context limits, training types (LoRA vs. Full), and multimodal capabilities, see the [Supported models](/autoscientist/supported-models/index.md) documentation.

## Wait for the run to complete

Wait for the run, then inspect its [status and results](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/get/index.md):

```
run = client.autoscientist.wait_for_completion(run.id)

if run.status != "succeeded":
    raise RuntimeError(f"{run.status}: {run.error}")

print(f"Best win rate: {run.best_win_rate}")
```

## Download the model

`download_available` confirms that AutoScientist produced a checkpoint. The [download endpoint](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/download/index.md) streams the archive without loading it into memory:

```
if not run.download_available:
    raise RuntimeError("The checkpoint is not available for download")

with client.autoscientist.with_streaming_response.download(run.id) as response:
    response.stream_to_file("best-checkpoint.tgz")
```

See the [`create` reference](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create/index.md) for all run parameters and the [`get` reference](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/get/index.md) for response fields.

[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist/data-augmentation/ | Type: docs | Title: Data augmentation | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Data augmentation

> Add domain-specific and general-purpose rows before AutoScientist training begins.

[Augmentation](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create/index.md) is optional, but recommended when a dataset is small or lacks diversity. AutoScientist can add two independent types of rows before its training iterations begin:

- **Domain rows** add examples specific to the dataset’s domain. Existing rows count toward the recommended 20,000-domain-row target.
- **General rows** add diverse examples that help the model retain broader capabilities.

This is the same curated-pool operation as [`datasets.augment`](/adaptive-data/expand-data/index.md). Use that helper when you want a new dataset before training. Use `augmentation_domain_rows` and `augmentation_general_rows` on `create` when you want the rows applied as part of the training run.

## Calculate the additions

The following request targets at least 20,000 domain rows and adds 8,000 general rows:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

dataset_id = "dataset_abc123"
dataset = client.datasets.get(dataset_id=dataset_id)

domain_rows_to_add = max(0, 20_000 - (dataset.row_count or 0))

run = client.autoscientist.create(
    dataset_id=dataset_id,
    augmentation_domain_rows=domain_rows_to_add,
    augmentation_general_rows=8_000,
)
print(run.id, run.status)
```

This produces up to 28,000 training rows: the existing dataset plus enough domain rows to reach 20,000, followed by 8,000 general rows. If the dataset already contains at least 20,000 rows, `domain_rows_to_add` is zero.

Omit either augmentation parameter to skip that type of addition. AutoScientist prices and sizes each requested expansion before training. See the [`create` API reference](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create/index.md) for current limits and request fields.

## Augment preference data

For a text DPO run, set `training_method="alignment"` on the same request. AutoScientist produces preference-shaped additions, and those additions count toward the minimum of 12,000 effective preference pairs:

```
run = client.autoscientist.create(
    dataset_id=dataset_id,
    training_method="alignment",
    augmentation_domain_rows=domain_rows_to_add,
    augmentation_general_rows=8_000,
)
```
title: Data augmentation

[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist/download-the-model/ | Type: docs | Title: Download the model | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Download the model

> Stream the best AutoScientist checkpoint to a local archive.

AutoScientist [downloads the checkpoint](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/download/index.md) from the best iteration, which is not necessarily the final iteration. The endpoint streams a compressed tar archive rather than returning a presigned URL.

For `training_method="alignment"`, the download belongs to the DPO stage.

## Stream the checkpoint

[Retrieve the run](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/get/index.md) first and verify that it completed and produced a downloadable checkpoint:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

run_id = "autoscientist_run_abc123"
run = client.autoscientist.get(run_id)

if run.status == "failed":
    raise RuntimeError(f"failed: {run.error}")
if run.status != "succeeded":
    raise RuntimeError(f"Run is not complete: {run.status}")
if not run.download_available:
    raise RuntimeError("The checkpoint is not available for download")

with client.autoscientist.with_streaming_response.download(run.id) as response:
    response.stream_to_file("best-checkpoint.tgz")
```

Using the streaming response avoids loading a large model archive into memory.

## Inspect the archive

`tar` detects the archive’s compression:

Terminal window

```
mkdir -p best-checkpoint
tar xf best-checkpoint.tgz -C best-checkpoint
```

A LoRA checkpoint typically contains:

```
adapter_config.json
adapter_model.safetensors
tokenizer.json
trainer_state.json
...
```

To publish manually to Hugging Face, create an empty model repository and upload the extracted files through its web interface or tooling. Keep the archive private if the weights or tokenizer contain proprietary information.

See the [`download` API reference](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/download/index.md) for the current response.
title: Download the model

[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist/interpreting-results/ | Type: docs | Title: Interpreting results | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Interpreting results

> Retrieve an AutoScientist run and understand its win rate and training diagnostics.

## Retrieve a completed run

Use the run ID returned when you [create the run](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create/index.md), then [retrieve its current results](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/get/index.md):

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

run_id = "autoscientist_run_abc123"
run = client.autoscientist.get(run_id)

if run.status in {"pending", "running"}:
    run = client.autoscientist.wait_for_completion(run.id)

if run.status == "failed":
    raise RuntimeError(f"failed: {run.error}")
if run.status != "succeeded":
    raise RuntimeError(f"Run ended with status: {run.status}")

print(f"Iterations: {run.iterations_completed}/{run.max_iterations}")
print(f"Training method: {run.training_method}")
print(f"Best win rate: {run.best_win_rate}")
print(f"Checkpoint available: {run.download_available}")
```

The app’s results page also shows the trained model ID, **Weights export**, and **AutoScientist Config**. Response fields can evolve; use the [`get` API reference](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/get/index.md) for the exact SDK field that corresponds to an app value.

### DPO stage transitions

A run returned with `training_method="alignment"` includes an SFT stage followed by DPO under the same public ID. During the handoff between stages, `status` remains `running`, `best_win_rate` and other best-result fields can be null, and `download_available` is false. Continue polling; once DPO starts, the public status, iterations, metrics, and artifact availability describe that stage.

## Training win rate

The **Training Winrates** chart compares the base model with the adapted model on evaluations derived from your dataset. A 70% adapted-model win rate means the adapted model won roughly 70% of the head-to-head comparisons.

`best_win_rate` is the best result across all iterations. A `succeeded` run may have reached `target_win_rate` early or simply completed `max_iterations`, so compare those values rather than treating success as proof that the target was reached.

## Train and evaluation metrics

The charts plot standard diagnostics over training steps:

- **Loss** measures prediction error. Falling training and evaluation loss generally indicates learning; falling training loss paired with worsening evaluation loss can indicate overfitting. For DPO, loss reflects how strongly the model separates chosen responses from rejected responses relative to the reference policy; compare it with evaluation win rate rather than interpreting it alone.
- **Learning rate** shows the optimizer’s step size over time and reflects the configured warmup and schedule.
- **Gradient norm** measures the overall gradient magnitude. Sudden spikes can indicate unstable updates, while a stable curve suggests optimization has settled.
title: Interpreting results

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist/interpreting-results/ | Type: docs | Title: Interpreting results | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Read these curves together. A smooth loss curve is not enough if win rate is flat, and a strong win rate can still accompany unstable training diagnostics that deserve investigation.

## Common issues

- **Flat or negative win rate:** use a model with enough capacity, consider more epochs, and evaluate whether [augmentation](/autoscientist/data-augmentation/index.md) should bring the domain dataset toward 20,000 rows.
- **No downloadable checkpoint:** confirm the run succeeded and `download_available` is true before following [Download the model](/autoscientist/download-the-model/index.md) or calling the [`download` method](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/download/index.md).
- **DPO metrics temporarily missing:** if the run is still `running`, it can be moving from SFT to DPO. Continue polling the same run ID.
- **Unclear run state:** retrieve the run and inspect `status`; `pending` is queued, `running` is active, and `failed` includes the reason in `error`.
- **Need original rather than adapted rows:** create a [raw dataset](/autoscientist/run-on-non-adapted-data/index.md) or select original columns when configuring the run.
title: Interpreting results

[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist/overview/ | Type: docs | Title: Overview | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Overview

> Understand what AutoScientist builds and how its iterative training loop works.

AutoScientist automates the research loop behind model training and alignment. You choose the outcome; AutoScientist optimizes the data and [training recipe](/autoscientist/recommended-hyperparameters/index.md), trains a model, evaluates it, and repeats until the run reaches its goal or exhausts its iterations.

Start with a dataset that has completed an [Adaptive Data](/adaptive-data/overview/index.md) run. If your source is already a training-ready prompt/completion dataset, you can instead [run on non-adapted data](/autoscientist/run-on-non-adapted-data/index.md).

![Select a dataset for AutoScientist](/auto-scientist/ASEX1.png)

## What you can build

- **Instruction datasets** pair prompts with expected completions for supervised fine-tuning.
- **Preference-pair datasets** compare chosen and rejected completions for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).

Set `training_method="instruction"` for supervised fine-tuning or `training_method="alignment"` for the SFT → DPO pipeline when you [create a run](/autoscientist/running-autoscientist/index.md). Alignment requires a dataset prepared as `preference_pairs`; pass the method explicitly rather than relying on saved app settings.

## How the loop works

Each run cycles through four stages:

1. **[Data optimization](/autoscientist/data-augmentation/index.md)** adds optional domain-targeted and general-purpose rows to improve diversity and reduce overfitting.
2. **[Training](/autoscientist/running-autoscientist/index.md)** runs SFT or DPO with the selected model, LoRA or full fine-tuning, and the current hyperparameter recipe.
3. **[Evaluation](/autoscientist/interpreting-results/index.md)** measures the iteration against `target_win_rate` and captures training diagnostics such as loss, learning rate, and gradient norm.
4. **Hyperparameter adjustment** analyzes the evaluation and revises the recipe for the next iteration.

The loop stops when it reaches `target_win_rate` or completes `max_iterations`. A `succeeded` status can mean either condition, so inspect `best_win_rate` after completion.

## Next steps

- [Configure data augmentation](/autoscientist/data-augmentation/index.md)
- [Create and monitor a run](/autoscientist/running-autoscientist/index.md)
- [Interpret the results](/autoscientist/interpreting-results/index.md)
- [Download the best checkpoint](/autoscientist/download-the-model/index.md)
- [Review supported models and training limits](/autoscientist/supported-models/index.md)
- Browse every request and response field in the [`create` API reference](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create/index.md)

# Hyperparameters

> Understand the training recipe AutoScientist selects and iterates on automatically.

AutoScientist [proposes a complete training recipe](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/recommend_hyperparams/index.md) before training, then evaluates and adjusts the recipe across iterations. **For most runs, keep the recommended values unchanged.** AutoScientist is optimized to select these values together and improve them based on measured results.

Changing individual hyperparameters is not recommended. An override can prevent AutoScientist from exploring the configuration it would otherwise select and can reduce training quality. Override a value only when you have a specific experimental or infrastructure constraint.

## Hyperparameter reference

`training_method` is a top-level `create` argument (`instruction` or `alignment`). The remaining fields below are keys inside `hyperparams`.

### General training

These hyperparameters apply to both SFT and DPO runs.

### LoRA

These hyperparameters configure Low-Rank Adaptation and are only applicable when `training_type` is `"lora"`. In alignment (SFT → DPO) pipelines, LoRA settings are frozen from the winning SFT iteration and cannot be changed during DPO.

| Hyperparameter           | Definition                                                                                                                                              | Valid Values                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lora_r`                 | Rank of the LoRA adapter matrices. Controls adapter capacity — higher ranks can represent more complex adaptations but require more memory and compute. | Power-of-2 integer, `1`–`64`                                           |
| `lora_alpha`             | Scaling factor for the LoRA adapter’s contribution to the base model. Must be `1×` or `2×` the value of `lora_r`.                                       | Power-of-2 integer (`1×` or `2× lora_r`)                               |
| `lora_dropout`           | Dropout probability applied to LoRA layers during training. Adds regularization to reduce overfitting.                                                  | Float, `0.0`–`1.0` (typically `0.0`–`0.1`)                             |
| `lora_trainable_modules` | Which model layers receive LoRA adapters. `"all-linear"` targets every linear layer; alternatively, specify a comma-separated list of module names.     | `"all-linear"` or comma-separated list (e.g. `"q_proj,v_proj,o_proj"`) |

### SFT specific

| Hyperparameter    | Definition                                                                                                                                                                   | Valid Values      |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `train_on_inputs` | Whether training loss is computed over prompt tokens in addition to completion tokens. Setting to `false` masks the prompt so the model only learns to generate completions. | `true` \| `false` |

These hyperparameters apply only to preference-based (DPO) training. They are inert for SFT runs.

| `dpo_beta`                          | Controls how far the model is allowed to drift from the reference model. Lower values (around `0.1`) update more aggressively toward the preferred output; higher values (around `0.7`) stay closer to the reference.                                                                                                                                                        | Float, `0.05`–`0.9`                 |
| `dpo_normalize_logratios_by_length` | Normalizes log ratios by sample length during loss calculation. Automatically set to `true` when `simpo_gamma` is above `0`. Changing this flag alters the effective scale of `dpo_beta`; treat a change as a major intervention.                                                                                                                                            | `true` \| `false`                   |
| `rpo_alpha`                         | Weight of an auxiliary negative log-likelihood (NLL) loss on preferred responses, added on top of the standard DPO loss (Regularized Preference Optimization). Counteracts likelihood displacement — the failure mode where chosen-response probability drifts downward even as the reward margin grows. Set to `0.0` to disable. **Cannot be combined with `simpo_gamma`.** | Float ≥ `0.0` (typical `0.1`–`1.0`) |
| `simpo_gamma`                       | Target reward margin from Simple Preference Optimization. Above `0.0`, the objective becomes reference-free and length-normalized: the chosen response must beat the rejected response by at least this margin. Raise `dpo_beta` alongside it since SimPO typically calls for a substantially larger beta. Set to `0.0` to disable. **Cannot be combined with `rpo_alpha`.** | Float ≥ `0.0` (typical `0.3`–`1.6`) |

## Review in the app

The proposed fields are editable, but the default workflow is to review and accept them:
title: Hyperparameters

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist/recommended-hyperparameters/ | Type: docs | Title: Hyperparameters | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
1. Review the model, algorithm, and generated recipe.
2. Keep the recommended values unless a known constraint requires an override.
3. Inspect the final **AutoScientist Config** JSON before confirming.
4. Let AutoScientist evaluate and refine the recipe across iterations.
5. After training, compare win rate and diagnostics as described in [Interpreting results](/autoscientist/interpreting-results/index.md).

## Advanced: Apply API overrides

API overrides are an advanced escape hatch for controlled experiments or hard requirements. The SDK accepts the training objective through top-level `training_method`, the base model through top-level `model`, and recipe overrides through `hyperparams`. `training_type` is a field inside `hyperparams`, not a top-level argument.

If an override is necessary, avoid unsupported key names: copy a valid `hyperparams` object from the current app configuration or construct it from the current [`create` API schema](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create/index.md), save it as `hyperparams.json`, and pass it unchanged:

```
import json
from pathlib import Path

from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

dataset_id = "dataset_abc123"
hyperparams = json.loads(Path("hyperparams.json").read_text())

run = client.autoscientist.create(
    dataset_id=dataset_id,
    training_method="alignment",
    hyperparams={
        **hyperparams,
        "training_type": "lora",
        "dpo_beta": 0.1,
    },
)
print(run.id, run.status)
```

Unset hyperparameter keys remain under platform control. To enforce a specific model, review the [supported models](/autoscientist/supported-models/index.md), list the currently available IDs, and pass one through `model`:

```
response = client.autoscientist.list_models()
for model in response.models:
    print(model.id)
```

Prefer leaving `model` and `hyperparams` unset so AutoScientist can choose and iterate on them automatically. See [Running AutoScientist](/autoscientist/running-autoscientist/index.md) for the complete request and status workflow.

# Run on non-adapted data

> Upload training-ready prompt/completion data for supervised fine-tuning.

Use [raw dataset processing](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/create/index.md) when a tabular file already contains training-ready prompt and completion columns and you want AutoScientist to train on those rows as-is with SFT. This skips Adaptive Data’s adaptation pipeline.

For best results, [adapt your data first](/adaptive-data/overview/index.md). Use raw processing only when training on the original rows is intentional.

Raw processing does not mark a dataset as `preference_pairs`. For DPO, first complete an [Adaptive Data preference-pair run](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data#generate-preference-pairs/index.md), then [create a DPO run](/autoscientist/running-autoscientist#train-on-preference-pairs/index.md).

Raw processing supports CSV, JSON, JSONL, and Parquet files. Set `processing_mode` to `raw` and [map both required source columns](/adaptive-data/select-columns/index.md) when creating the dataset.

## Upload and train

This example uploads a CSV whose `instruction` and `response` columns contain the training pairs:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

dataset = client.datasets.upload_file(
    "training_data.csv",
    processing_mode="raw",
    column_mapping={
        "prompt": "instruction",
        "completion": "response",
    },
)

client.datasets.wait_for_completion(dataset.dataset_id)

run = client.autoscientist.create(dataset_id=dataset.dataset_id)
run = client.autoscientist.wait_for_completion(run.id)

if run.status == "failed":
    raise RuntimeError(f"failed: {run.error}")
if run.status != "succeeded":
    raise RuntimeError(f"Run ended with status: {run.status}")

print(run.id, run.best_win_rate)
```

Do not call `client.datasets.adapt` for this workflow: raw processing makes the uploaded dataset ready for AutoScientist directly. The `column_mapping` above refers to the original file headers; an AutoScientist `column_mapping`, if supplied later, refers to the processed dataset schema.

See [Running AutoScientist](/autoscientist/running-autoscientist/index.md) for polling, cancellation, and status details. For endpoint details, see the [`datasets.create`](/api/python/resources/datasets/methods/create/index.md) and [`autoscientist.create`](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create/index.md) references.
title: Run on non-adapted data

# Running AutoScientist

> Create, monitor, and handle an AutoScientist training run with the Python SDK.

## Create a run

The SDK reads `ADAPTION_API_KEY` from the environment. Call [`autoscientist.create`](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/create/index.md) with the prepared dataset:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

dataset_id = "dataset_abc123"
run = client.autoscientist.create(dataset_id=dataset_id)
print(run.id, run.status)  # pending
```
title: Running AutoScientist

| --------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| `max_iterations`            | No       | From 1 through 5.                                                                                                                                                                      |

title: Running AutoScientist

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist/running-autoscientist/ | Type: docs | Title: Running AutoScientist | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
`column_mapping` is validated against the **adapted dataset’s schema**, not the uploaded file’s original headers. Adaptation can add columns such as `enhanced_prompt`. A mapping to a missing column fails with `Selected column '...' for prompt is not in this dataset`.

### Train on preference pairs

First, complete an [Adaptive Data preference-pair run](/adaptive-data/configure-adaptive-data#generate-preference-pairs/index.md). A preference-pair dataset does not by itself select alignment, so set `training_method` explicitly:

```
run = client.autoscientist.create(
    dataset_id=dataset_id,
    training_method="alignment",
)
print(run.id, run.training_method)  # alignment
```

Standard Adaptive Data output can be inferred without `column_mapping`. If the adapted schema instead exposes separate custom columns, map all three roles:

```
run = client.autoscientist.create(
    dataset_id=dataset_id,
    training_method="alignment",
    column_mapping={
        "prompt": "question",
        "chosen": "preferred_answer",
        "rejected": "other_answer",
    },
)
```

DPO requires at least **12,000 effective preference pairs**, including requested augmentation. SFT requires at least 1,000 effective rows. Selecting `alignment` does not convert another dataset type: the API resolves the run to `instruction` unless the dataset was prepared as `preference_pairs`. Read `run.training_method` to confirm the resolved objective.

AutoScientist presents alignment as one run, but trains an SFT adapter before the DPO stage. The public run ID and resolved `training_method="alignment"` remain stable across both stages. During the handoff, the run stays `running`, metrics can be temporarily unavailable, and `download_available` is false. A cancellation request during this brief handoff can return `409`; retry after an iteration becomes active.

## Wait for completion

[Run status](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/get/index.md) is `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.

```
from adaption import TrainingTimeout

try:
    run = client.autoscientist.wait_for_completion(run.id)
except TrainingTimeout as exc:
    print(exc.resource_id, exc.last_status)
    raise

if run.status == "failed":
    raise RuntimeError(f"failed: {run.error}")
if run.status != "succeeded":
    raise RuntimeError(f"Run ended with status: {run.status}")

print(run.iterations_completed, run.max_iterations, run.best_win_rate)
```

`wait_for_completion` backs off from 10 to 60 seconds and has a four-hour default timeout. A timeout stops waiting, not training. Call it again with the same run ID to resume tracking.

To control the polling schedule yourself:

```
import time

while True:
    run = client.autoscientist.get(run.id)
    print(run.status, run.iterations_completed, run.best_win_rate)
title: Running AutoScientist

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/autoscientist/running-autoscientist/ | Type: docs | Title: Running AutoScientist | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
if run.status == "succeeded":
        break
    if run.status == "failed":
        raise RuntimeError(f"failed: {run.error}")
    if run.status == "cancelled":
        raise RuntimeError("Run was cancelled")

    time.sleep(30)
```

A successful run either reached `target_win_rate` or used its final iteration. [Compare `best_win_rate` with the target](/autoscientist/interpreting-results/index.md) to determine which occurred. Use [`client.autoscientist.cancel(run.id)`](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/cancel/index.md) to stop a run in flight.

## Constrain model size

In the app, **Tiny AutoScientist** limits selection to models under 10B parameters. With the SDK, review the [supported models](/autoscientist/supported-models/index.md), list the currently available models, and pass an eligible ID explicitly:

```
response = client.autoscientist.list_models()
for model in response.models:
    print(model.id)

model_id = input("Eligible model ID: ").strip()
run = client.autoscientist.create(
    dataset_id=dataset_id,
    model=model_id,
)
```

Model availability and metadata can change. Confirm the current values with [`autoscientist.list_models`](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/list_models/index.md) rather than inferring model size from its ID.

# Supported models

> Base models available to AutoScientist and the per-model limits for context length, batch size, and LoRA rank.

Every model below can be passed as the `model` field when [creating an AutoScientist run](/autoscientist/running-autoscientist/index.md). The runtime model list is authoritative; use this page as a planning reference.

```
response = client.autoscientist.list_models()
for model in response.models:
    print(model.id, model.api_model_size, model.methods, model.training_types)
```

See the [`autoscientist.list_models` API reference](/api/python/resources/autoscientist/methods/list_models/index.md) for the current response schema.

You do not need to select a model. Omit `model` and AutoScientist selects one that supports the requested `training_method`. The resolved model ID is returned on the run.

| `google/gemma-3-27b-it-VLM`                          | 32768         | 24576         | 8               | 8               | 1                     | 64               |
| `google/gemma-4-31B-it-VLM`                          | 24576         | 12288         | 8               | 8               | 1                     | 64               |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`                                    | 131072        | 65536         | 8               | 8               | 1                     | 64               |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`                                    | 65536         | 49152         | 8               | 8               | 1                     | 64               |

### Batch size

Each model has one valid batch size. `batch_size` defaults to `"max"`, which resolves to that model-specific value. **Leaving it unchanged is the right choice for almost every run.** Supplying another integer causes the launch to fail after the job is accepted.

Models use gradient accumulation when a larger effective batch is useful.

```
# Recommended: let AutoScientist resolve the model and batch size.
run = client.autoscientist.create(dataset_id=dataset_id)

# Advanced: pin a model and its required batch size.
run = client.autoscientist.create(
    dataset_id=dataset_id,
    model="openai/gpt-oss-20b",
    hyperparams={"batch_size": 1},
)
```

### LoRA rank

`lora_r` accepts values from 1 through 64 for every model on this page. `lora_alpha` must be exactly one or two times `lora_r`; the API cross-checks the values when both are supplied in the same request.

## Row count

AutoScientist enforces the following minimum effective dataset sizes (base rows + augmentation):

| Training method   | Minimum rows | Applies to                          |
| ----------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------- |
| SFT (instruction) | **1,000**    | All models                          |
| DPO (preference)  | **12,000**   | All models                          |
| Any method        | **10,000**   | Gemma (≥ 26B), Qwen (≥ 35B), NVIDIA |

Text datasets can use augmentation to reach a minimum. Multimodal datasets cannot currently be augmented, so they must already contain enough processed rows. AutoScientist treats **20,000 rows** as a recommended quality target, not a hard launch requirement.

## Context length and your data

Training context is the maximum sequence length used during fine-tuning. It is shorter than the serving context. Rows longer than the training limit are truncated rather than rejected.

DPO context can be shorter than SFT context. Before pinning a model for DPO, confirm that `DPO` appears in its runtime `methods` list and use the DPO context column above.

# Generate a model response

> Choose a model, continue conversations, stream output, use tools, and send image inputs with the Responses API.

Use `responses.create` to generate text from a model. This guide covers choosing a model, keeping conversation state, streaming output, adding tools, and sending image inputs.

## Choose a model

### Use a model directly

Pass a model identifier as `model`. Set its instructions and tools on the request:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    instructions="You are a concise technical writer.",
    input="Explain what an API rate limit is.",
)

print(response.output_text)
```

### Use a stack

Pass `stack:<slug>` as `model` to call one of your stacks. The request uses the stack’s model, tools, datasets, and memory setting:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="stack:support-assistant",
    input="Summarize this week's open escalations.",
)

print(response.output_text)
```

Request parameters can override stack defaults:

- An explicit `tools` array replaces the stack’s default tool set. Pass `tools=[]` to disable tools for the request.
- `agentic_memory` overrides the stack’s memory setting.
- A `file_search` entry without `dataset_ids` searches the stack’s ready indexed datasets. Add `dataset_ids` to search specific datasets instead.

See [Key concepts](/inference-stacks/key-concepts/index.md) for how each default is applied.

## Manage conversation state

Each request is independent unless you send earlier turns in `input` or continue from a stored response.

### Send the conversation history

Append the response’s output to your input list, add the next user message, and send the complete history:

```
from typing import Any

from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

history: list[Any] = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Tell me a joke about databases."},
]

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input=history,
)
print(response.output_text)

history += response.output
history.append({"role": "user", "content": "Explain why it's funny."})

second = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input=history,
)
print(second.output_text)
```

### Continue from a stored response

Set `store=True`, then pass the response ID as `previous_response_id`. Adaption prepends the stored conversation, so the next request needs only the new turn:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input="Tell me a joke about databases.",
    store=True,
)
print(response.output_text)

second = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    previous_response_id=response.id,
    input="Explain why it's funny.",
    store=True,
)
print(second.output_text)
```
title: Generate a model response

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/inference-stacks/generate-a-model-response/ | Type: docs | Title: Generate a model response | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Unlike OpenAI, Adaption does not store responses by default. Set `store=True` on every response you may continue from. Stored responses are retained for 30 days.

Retrieve or delete a stored response by ID:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

stored = client.responses.retrieve("resp_123")
print(stored.output_text)

client.responses.delete("resp_123")
```

## Stream a response

Pass `stream=True` to receive server-sent events while the response is generated. Text arrives in `response.output_text.delta` events:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

stream = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input="Write a short poem about the ocean.",
    stream=True,
)

for event in stream:
    if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
        print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
    elif event.type == "response.completed":
        print()
```

Common events include:

- **`response.created`** — the response starts.
- **`response.output_text.delta`** — the model generates more text.
- **`response.file_search_call.completed`** — a file search finishes.
- **`response.completed`** — the response finishes.
- **`error`** — the request fails.

## Add tools

Tools let a model call functions and services while it generates a response. The Responses API supports four kinds:

- **Function tools** run in your code.
- **Remote MCP servers** are MCP servers you host or choose.
- **Hosted tools**, such as `file_search`, run on Adaption.
- **Connectors** are services you connect in the Adaption app, such as Slack or Linear.

Adaption runs remote MCP, hosted, and connector tool calls and returns the final answer. Function tool calls are returned for your code to run.

### Function tools

Define a function with a JSON schema for its arguments. When the model calls it, the response ends with a `function_call` item. Run the function, then send its result back as a `function_call_output` item:

```
import json
from typing import Any

from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

tools: list[Any] = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather for a city.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["city"],
        },
    }
]

def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    return f"It is 18°C and sunny in {city}."

history: list[Any] = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Paris?"},
]

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input=history,
    tools=tools,
)

history += response.output
for item in response.output:
    if item.type == "function_call":
        arguments = json.loads(item.arguments or "{}")
        history.append(
            {
                "type": "function_call_output",
                "call_id": item.call_id,
                "output": get_weather(**arguments),
            }
        )

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/inference-stacks/generate-a-model-response/ | Type: docs | Title: Generate a model response | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
final = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input=history,
    tools=tools,
)
print(final.output_text)
```

### Remote MCP servers

Give the model a remote MCP server by URL. Adaption connects to the server, lists its tools, and runs the calls:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input="What transport protocols does the MCP specification support?",
    tools=[
        {
            "type": "mcp",
            "server_label": "deepwiki",
            "server_url": "https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp",
            "allowed_tools": ["ask_question"],
            "require_approval": "never",
        }
    ],
)

print(response.output_text)
```

- `authorization` is sent to the server as its `Authorization` header. Adaption does not store, log, or return it.
- `allowed_tools` limits which server tools the model can call.
- `require_approval` controls which calls wait for your approval.

Remote MCP calls require approval by default. Set `require_approval` to `"never"` only for servers you trust.

When a call needs approval, the response ends with an `mcp_approval_request`. Replay the response output with an `mcp_approval_response` to continue:

```
from typing import Any

from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

tools: list[Any] = [
    {
        "type": "mcp",
        "server_label": "deepwiki",
        "server_url": "https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp",
    }
]
history: list[Any] = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "What does the MCP specification say about auth?",
    },
]

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input=history,
    tools=tools,
)

history += response.output
for item in response.output:
    if item.type == "mcp_approval_request":
        history.append(
            {
                "type": "mcp_approval_response",
                "approval_request_id": item.id,
                "approve": True,
            }
        )

final = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input=history,
    tools=tools,
)
print(final.output_text)
```

### Hosted tools

Hosted tools run on Adaption and need no connector setup. Use `file_search` to ground answers in your authorized, indexed datasets:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input="What return window do we offer on electronics?",
    tools=[{"type": "file_search", "dataset_ids": ["DATASET_ID"]}],
)

print(response.output_text)
```

`file_search` uses semantic search to retrieve relevant rows, passes them to the model as context, and adds citations to the response.

Web search and code execution are upcoming hosted tools.

### Connectors

Connectors use the connections configured in the Adaption app. Reference one by its `server_label`; no credential is needed in the request:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input="List the Linear issues assigned to me that are due this week.",
    tools=[{"type": "mcp", "server_label": "linear"}],

print(response.output_text)

## Send image inputs

Multimodal models, such as `qwen3.5-397b`, accept images alongside text. Send a message whose content contains `input_text` and `input_image` parts. The image can be a public URL or a base64 data URL:

```
import base64
from typing import Any

from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

with open("receipt.png", "rb") as file:
    image = base64.b64encode(file.read()).decode()

messages: list[Any] = [
    {
        "type": "message",
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "input_text", "text": "What is the total on this receipt?"},
            {
                "type": "input_image",
                "image_url": f"data:image/png;base64,{image}",
            },
        ],
    }
]

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input=messages,
)

print(response.output_text)
```

# Key concepts

> Understand stacks, tools and connectors, file search, and memory in the Adaption Responses API.

The Responses API builds on a few core concepts: stacks group a model with its tools and data, tools and connectors let the model act on external systems, file search grounds answers in your datasets, and memory carries useful context across turns.

## Stacks

A stack is a saved configuration of a model, tools, datasets, and memory. It provides defaults for API requests so that each request does not need to repeat the same configuration.

A stack defines:

- **Model** — the model that answers requests
- **Tools** — the connectors and hosted tools the model can call
- **Datasets** — the datasets available to `file_search`
- **Memory** — whether agentic memory is on by default

### Create and manage stacks

Create and manage stacks from [**Inference stacks**](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/inference-stacks) in the Adaption app. The API can call stacks but does not create or edit them.

### Call a stack

Pass `stack:<slug>` as the model. The request uses the stack’s model, tools, datasets, and memory setting:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="stack:support-assistant",
    input="Summarize this week's open escalations.",
)
```

A stack can be called only by the user who owns it, with an API key for the stack’s organization. The stack must also be active.

## Tools and connectors

Tools let a model fetch information and take actions during a response. Adaption runs the tool calls and returns the final answer along with each call the model made.

### Connect a connector

Open [**Settings → Connectors**](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings?tab=connectors), choose a connector, and select **Connect**. Adaption manages the authorization and stores the encrypted credentials, so you do not need to handle them in your code. The same connection works with the Responses API and Adaption Chat.

Connector availability depends on your account. List the tool catalog to see each connector’s `server_label` and whether you can use it:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

for tool in client.tools.list().data:
    print(tool.name, tool.server_label, tool.available)
```

Missing a connector? Email <support@adaptionlabs.ai>.

### Enable a connector on a stack

When a connector is enabled on a stack, it is available by default to requests that use that stack.

Pass `tools` to use a narrower set for one request. Pass an empty list to call the stack without tools:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

# Use only the Slack connector for this request
response = client.responses.create(
    model="stack:support-assistant",
    input="What did the team decide in #launch yesterday?",
    tools=[{"type": "mcp", "server_label": "slack"}],
)
title: Key concepts

text:
[Source: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/inference-stacks/key-concepts/ | Type: docs | Title: Key concepts | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
# Disable all tools for this request
response = client.responses.create(
    model="stack:support-assistant",
    input="Draft a friendly greeting.",
    tools=[],
)
```

A connector requested in `tools` must be enabled on the stack.

## File search

`file_search` lets a model search your datasets. The model decides when to search and how to phrase each query, can search more than once, and cites the rows it uses in its answer.

For a hosted model, pass the datasets to search:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input="What return window do we offer on electronics?",
    tools=[{"type": "file_search", "dataset_ids": ["DATASET_ID"]}],
)
```

For a stack, add `{"type": "file_search"}` to `tools` to search the stack’s ready indexed datasets. To search specific datasets instead, pass `dataset_ids` as you would for a hosted model.

### Prepare a dataset for search

A dataset must have a ready retrieval index before it can be searched. In the app, select the text columns to index. Indexing runs in the background, and the stack page shows its status.

### Search results in the response

Each search appears in the response’s `output` as a `file_search_call` item containing the model’s query and the rows it found. Citations appear as `file_citation` annotations on the response text and identify the source dataset and row.

Use `max_tool_calls` to limit the number of tool calls a response can make. When the limit is reached, the model answers with the information it already has.

## Memory

With agentic memory, a stack remembers useful context from earlier conversations, such as preferences, decisions, and facts about your work.

- **Scope** — memories are kept per user and per stack.
- **Creation** — memories are built in the background after a response completes, so a new memory is not available immediately.
- **Use** — before each response, Adaption adds relevant memories to the model’s instructions.
- **Management** — view, edit, and delete memories from the stack’s detail page in the app.

Memory follows the stack’s default setting. Override it for one request with `agentic_memory`:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="stack:support-assistant",
    input="Which customers did I say to prioritize?",
    agentic_memory=True,
)
```

Requests that do not call a stack do not use memory.

## Call a model or stack

Pass a model ID as `model` to call a hosted model directly. To call an inference stack, use `stack:<slug>`. The stack supplies its configured model, tools, datasets, and memory setting.

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()  # reads ADAPTION_API_KEY

response = client.responses.create(
    model="stack:your-stack-slug",
    input="Hello",
)

print(response.output_text)
```

Use a stack’s slug when possible. `stack:<uuid>` remains supported for existing callers.

## List available models

Model availability can vary by API key. Pass `type="hosted"` to list the hosted models available to your key without including inference stacks or harnesses:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

for model in client.models.list(type="hosted").data:
    print(model.id)
```

# Quickstart

> Create an Adaption API key, install the Python SDK, and generate your first model response.

The Responses API generates model output from text or a list of messages. This guide takes you from a new API key to your first response in a few minutes.

This guide requires Adaption Python SDK version 0.16.0 or later.

## Create and export an API key

1. [Sign in](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/auth) to Adaption.

2. Open [**Settings**](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings), then open [**API keys**](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings?tab=api_keys).

3. Create a key and copy it. You will not be able to view the key again.

4. Export the key as `ADAPTION_API_KEY`. The SDK reads this variable automatically:

   Terminal window

   ```
   export ADAPTION_API_KEY="pt_live_..."
   ```

Store API keys in environment variables or a secret manager. Do not commit them to source control.

## Install the SDK

Terminal window

```
pip install adaption
```

## Send a request

Call `responses.create` with a model and an input:

```
from adaption import Adaption

client = Adaption()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    input="Write a one-sentence bedtime story about a unicorn.",
)

print(response.output_text)
```

`output_text` joins the text from every message in the response’s `output` array. The full `output` array also includes any tool calls the model made.

To guide the model’s behavior, add `instructions`:

```
response = client.responses.create(
    model="qwen3.5-397b",
    instructions="You are a helpful assistant.",
    input="Hello!",
)
```

## Next steps

- Stream output as it is generated by passing `stream=True`.
- Continue a conversation with `store=True` and `previous_response_id`.
- Give the model tools, such as MCP servers and `file_search` over your adapted datasets.

See the [`responses.create` API reference](/api/python/resources/responses/methods/create/index.md) for all request parameters.
