# Adaption Plugin for Cursor

Connect Cursor to [Adaption](https://adaptionlabs.ai) for dataset management and fine-tuning workflows.

The plugin signs in to Adaption with OAuth: Cursor opens the Adaption sign-in
page in your browser, and no API key is needed.

## Installation

Pick the method that matches what you are doing:

| Method | Use when |
|--------|----------|
| [Cursor Marketplace](#from-the-cursor-marketplace) | The plugin is published. One click, Cursor handles updates. |
| [Git repository](#from-the-git-repository) | Rolling it out to a team before it is public. |
| [Local checkout](#local-development) | Developing or testing changes that are not pushed yet. |

Cursor resolves plugin sources through Git, so the first two methods install a
**committed and pushed** revision. A working tree on disk is only picked up by
the local-checkout method below.

### From the Cursor Marketplace

1. Open **Customize** in the sidebar
2. Search for **"adaption"**
3. Click **Install**
4. [Sign in](#sign-in)

### From the Git repository

Import the repository as a team marketplace — this is the recommended way to
install the plugin from source:

1. Open **Dashboard → Plugins & MCPs**
2. Under **Team Marketplaces**, click **Add Marketplace** → **Import from Repo**
3. Paste `https://github.com/adaptionlabs/adaption-cursor-plugin`
4. Add the `adaption` plugin, set **Marketplace Access**, and save
5. In Cursor, open **Customize**, find **adaption**, and click **Install**
6. [Sign in](#sign-in)

Cursor indexes a single commit from the branch the marketplace tracks. Push your
changes and click **Refresh** (or enable **Auto Refresh**) before expecting them
to appear.

### Local development

> Do not add the repository folder as a plugin source in **Customize**. Cursor
> stages plugin sources with a `git init` and fetch, which yields nothing for a
> plain directory. The plugin card still renders from the manifest, so it looks
> installed, but the plugin payload is empty: no skills and no MCP server. The
> plugin log reports `0 plugins loaded, 0 failures` with no visible error.

The supported way to load an unpublished checkout is Cursor's local plugin
directory, `~/.cursor/plugins/local`:

```bash
./scripts/install-local.sh
```

The script copies this checkout to `~/.cursor/plugins/local/adaption`. It copies
rather than symlinks on purpose — Cursor skips symlinks whose target resolves
outside that directory.

Then:

1. Run **Developer: Reload Window**
2. [Sign in](#sign-in)
3. Under **MCP servers**, confirm `adaption` is connected

Re-run the script and reload the window after every change. MCP servers do not
hot-reload.

`mcp.json` ships the production endpoint. To test against another environment,
point `url` at it before running the script, and revert before committing.

If the same MCP URL is also configured in your own `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, Cursor
lists only that entry and hides the plugin's server. Remove the duplicate to
test the plugin.

## Sign in

1. Open **Customize → MCPs**. The `adaption` server shows **Needs

2. Click **Authenticate**. Cursor opens the Adaption sign-in page in your
   browser
3. Choose the organization and click **Authorize**

The server switches to connected and lists its tools.

### Cursor CLI

The Cursor CLI signs in with OAuth too. In an `agent` session, run `/mcp`,
select the `adaption` server, and authenticate. The CLI opens the same sign-in
page in your browser.

### Using an API key instead

For environments with no browser to complete the sign-in, such as a CI runner,
skip the plugin's server and add one with an Adaption API key to
`~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Create the key at
[adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings?tab=api_keys):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "adaption": {
      "url": "https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:ADAPTION_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Features

### 📊 Dataset Management

- Import datasets from HuggingFace, Kaggle, or Google Sheets
- Run adaptation pipelines
- Augment, translate, and localize datasets
- Combine multiple datasets
- Export processed results

### 🎯 Fine-tuning

- Browse available base models
- Launch training jobs
- Monitor training progress

### 🔬 Invent

- Generate synthetic training datasets from natural language descriptions
- Explore available domains and subdomains
- Create domain-specific data with no seed data to start from

## Available Skills

| Skill | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `adaption-dataset` | Dataset import, processing, and transformation |
| `adaption-training` | AutoScientist training runs |
| `adaption-invent` | Synthetic data generation |

## Example Usage

Once installed, you can interact with Adaption through natural conversation:

> "Import this HuggingFace dataset and adapt it for fine-tuning"

> "Start fine-tuning on my adapted dataset and pick a suitable base model"

> "Generate 1000 customer service examples using Invent"

> "Check the status of my training job"

## Requirements

- Cursor IDE
- An Adaption account

- **Documentation**: [docs.adaptionlabs.ai](https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai)
- **Issues**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/adaptionlabs/adaption-cursor-plugin/issues)
- **Email**: support@adaptionlabs.ai

# Adaption Plugin for Hermes Agent

Connect [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) to
[Adaption](https://adaptionlabs.ai) for dataset management, fine-tuning, and
AutoScientist workflows.

The plugin is an [Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org) package, which
Hermes installs natively. It contains:

- **The Adaption MCP server**, which gives Hermes the tools. You sign in with
  your Adaption account in the browser the first time it starts.
- **Three skills** that teach Hermes how to use those tools.

## Installation

The plugin connects through [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote),
so it needs Node.js 20.18.1 or later and npm on your `PATH`.

### Hermes Desktop

Open **Capabilities → Plugins → Install from Git**, enter
`adaptionlabs/adaption-hermes-plugin`, keep the agent plugin checked, and
confirm. Then enable **adaption** in the plugins list.

Or open this link, which only opens a confirmation dialog in Hermes Desktop:

```
hermes://plugin/install?repo=adaptionlabs/adaption-hermes-plugin&enable=1
```

### Hermes CLI

```bash
hermes plugins install adaptionlabs/adaption-hermes-plugin --no-enable
hermes plugins enable adaption
```

### Sign in

Sign in once before your first session:

```bash
npx -y -p mcp-remote@0.1.49 mcp-remote-client \
  'https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/mcp?source=hermes-plugin' \
  --transport http-only --header X-Adaption-Source:hermes-plugin \
  --static-oauth-client-info '{"client_id":"adaption-hermes-plugin"}'
```

In PowerShell, run it on one line through `npx.cmd`, with the inner quotes
escaped:

```powershell
npx.cmd -y -p mcp-remote@0.1.49 mcp-remote-client 'https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/mcp?source=hermes-plugin' --transport http-only --header X-Adaption-Source:hermes-plugin --static-oauth-client-info '{\"client_id\":\"adaption-hermes-plugin\"}'
```

Your browser opens the Adaption sign-in page. Choose the organization and
click **Authorize**. The token is stored and refreshed, so the plugin's server
connects without a browser from then on. Start a new session, or run
`/reload-mcp` in a running one, and run `skills_list` to see the Adaption
skills.

If you skip this step, the server opens the sign-in page when a session
starts, but Hermes stops waiting for it after about a minute. If that happens,
run the command above, then `/reload-mcp`.

To sign out or switch to another organization, delete the stored token and
sign in again:

```bash
rm ~/.mcp-auth/mcp-remote-0.1.49/68a9ef231d47fe56f4f1b863f1349fa4_*
```

### Approvals

The plugin marks the server `untrusted`, so Hermes asks before every tool the
server does not mark read-only. Adaption marks the tools that list and inspect
datasets, runs, models, and domains as read-only; they run without asking.
Hermes asks before import, adaptation, augmentation, translation,
localization, combining datasets, dataset generation, and AutoScientist runs.
In cron jobs and other unattended runs, those tools are refused.

text:
[Source: https://github.com/adaptionlabs/adaption-hermes-plugin | Type: github_readme | Title: adaption-hermes-plugin README | Published: unknown | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Cost estimates use the same tools with `estimate: true`, so Hermes asks before
the estimate and again before the launch.

### Headless use with an API key

For CI or a gateway with no one to complete a browser sign-in, use an Adaption
API key instead. Create one at
[adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings](https://adaptionlabs.ai/app/settings?tab=api_keys),
then:

```bash
hermes mcp add adaption --url 'https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/mcp?source=hermes-plugin' --auth header
```

Answer yes when Hermes asks whether the server requires authentication, then
paste the API key when it asks for a bearer token. Hermes stores it in your
profile's `.env` as `MCP_ADAPTION_API_KEY`, not in `config.yaml`. To skip the
prompt, set `MCP_ADAPTION_API_KEY` in that `.env` before running the command.

A server named `adaption` in `config.yaml` replaces the plugin's server,
including its approval setting, so the skills keep working with the key. To
keep the approvals described above:

```bash
hermes config set mcp_servers.adaption.trust untrusted
```

### Connecting without Node.js

Hermes can also sign in to the server itself, without `mcp-remote`. Add it to
`config.yaml`, which replaces the plugin's server:

```bash
hermes config set mcp_servers.adaption.url 'https://api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai/api/v1/mcp?source=hermes-plugin'
hermes config set mcp_servers.adaption.headers.x-adaption-source hermes-plugin
hermes config set mcp_servers.adaption.auth oauth
hermes config set mcp_servers.adaption.oauth.client_id adaption-hermes-plugin
hermes mcp login adaption
```

In Hermes Desktop, open this link instead and click **Authenticate** on the
`adaption` server:

```
hermes://mcp/install?name=adaption&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2FwaS5wcm9kLmFkYXB0aW9ubGFicy5haS9hcGkvdjEvbWNwP3NvdXJjZT1oZXJtZXMtcGx1Z2luIiwiaGVhZGVycyI6eyJYLUFkYXB0aW9uLVNvdXJjZSI6Imhlcm1lcy1wbHVnaW4ifSwiYXV0aCI6Im9hdXRoIiwib2F1dGgiOnsiY2xpZW50X2lkIjoiYWRhcHRpb24taGVybWVzLXBsdWdpbiJ9fQ
```

The `oauth` block is required: Adaption does not support dynamic client
registration, which Hermes falls back to without it. If you set the server up
this way before version 0.3.0 of the plugin, it keeps working; remove it with
`hermes mcp remove adaption` to switch to the plugin's server.

### Local development

Hermes discovers packages in `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/`. Copy a checkout
there to test changes before they are pushed:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/adaptionlabs/adaption-hermes-plugin.git
rsync -a --delete --exclude .git adaption-hermes-plugin/ ~/.hermes/plugins/adaption/
hermes plugins enable adaption
```

Re-run `rsync` and start a new session after every change.

## Features

### 📊 Dataset Management (11 tools)

- **Import** datasets from HuggingFace, Kaggle, or Google Sheets
- **Adapt** datasets with Adaption's processing pipeline
- **Augment** datasets with synthetic domain/general rows
- **Translate** and **localize** dataset content
- **Combine** multiple datasets
- Get **export links** for processed results

### 🎯 Fine-tuning (5 tools)

- Browse available **base models**
- Get **hyperparameter recommendations**
- Launch **AutoScientist training runs**
- Monitor **training progress** and results

### 🔬 Invent (2 tools)

- Explore available **domains and subdomains**
- **Generate synthetic datasets** from natural language descriptions

## Available Skills

| Skill | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `adaption-dataset` | Dataset import, processing, and transformation workflows |
| `adaption-training` | AutoScientist training run management |
| `adaption-invent` | Synthetic data generation with Invent |

## Example Usage

> "List my Adaption datasets"

> "Import this HuggingFace dataset and adapt it for fine-tuning"

> "Start fine-tuning on my adapted dataset and pick a suitable base model"

> "Generate 1000 customer service examples using Invent"

> "Check the status of my training job"

## What this plugin does on your machine

- It runs the pinned `mcp-remote@0.1.49` through `npx`, which downloads it
  from npm on first use. On first sign-in it opens a browser and a local
  callback port, and it stores the OAuth tokens under `~/.mcp-auth/`.
- Every tool call goes to `api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai` and acts on your Adaption
  account. The tool set is served by Adaption at run time and is not covered
  by the pinned commit. Datasets you import or generate are processed by
  Adaption.
- Adaptation, augmentation, translation, localization, dataset generation, and
  AutoScientist training runs spend Adaption credits. Hermes asks before each
  of those calls (see [Approvals](#approvals)), and the skills tell Hermes to
  request a cost estimate first.
- The skills are Markdown instructions. The plugin ships no Python code, hooks,
  or background processes beyond the `mcp-remote` bridge while a session runs.

## Requirements

- Hermes Agent 0.21.6 or later (`hermes update` to get the latest)
- Node.js 20.18.1 or later and npm, unless you connect without Node.js
- An Adaption account

## Support

- **Documentation**: [docs.adaptionlabs.ai](https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai)
- **Issues**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/adaptionlabs/adaption-hermes-plugin/issues)
- **Email**: support@adaptionlabs.ai

text:
[Source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/adaptionlabs/preference-pairs | Type: huggingface_page | Title: adaptionlabs/preference-pairs · Datasets at Hugging Face | Published: 2026-08-03 | Retrieved: 2026-11-17]
Reasoning-Augmented Preference Pairs
140,582 preference pairs across 6 languages and 8 domains, each chosen response paired with a step-by-step reasoning trace.
Every row includes a chosen/rejected preference pair and a reasoning trace behind the chosen response. This supports DPO training on the preference signal and reasoning distillation from the traces, together or separately. Rows come from 13 public instruction and reasoning datasets, filtered to HARD and MEDIUM difficulty, with the five non-English languages holding roughly 10% each.
Highlights
- Reasoning traces. Each row pairs chosen/rejected with a reasoning_trace for the chosen response. The trace explains the preferred answer, not the rejected one.
- Difficulty filtered. HARD and MEDIUM rows only. EASY rows are dropped during selection.
- Multilingual. English plus Arabic, French, Hindi, Mandarin, and Spanish, at roughly 10% each for the five non-English languages.
- Source context. 5 of the 13 sources include the underlying context (financial filing, clinical record, article) in the same language as the prompt.
- Domain coverage. 8 buckets: general instruction-following, medical, finance, science, math, code, safety, and other.
Quick start
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("your-org/preference-pairs")  # replace with the published repo id
print(ds["train"][0])
Dataset summary
| Rows | 140,582 | 
| Columns | prompt, context, chosen, rejected, reasoning_trace, language, domain, source_dataset | 
| Languages | English + Arabic, French, Hindi, Mandarin, Spanish (~10% each) | 
| Domains | 8 buckets: general instruction-following, medical, finance, science, math, code, safety, other (legal and summarization fold into other) | 
| Difficulty | HARD and MEDIUM only | 
Columns
| Column | Description | 
|---|---|
| prompt | The task prompt, as sourced from the originating dataset. No separate rewrite or enhancement step this round (see What's different from v1). | 
| context | Supporting source document or data referenced by the prompt (financial filing, clinical record, article, etc.), in the same language as prompt. Present for 5 of the 13 sources. | 
| chosen | The preferred response to the prompt. | 
| rejected | The dispreferred response to the same prompt. Pair with chosen for DPO-style preference training. | 
| reasoning_trace | A step-by-step reasoning trace behind the chosen response specifically, not rejected. | 
| language | Detected language of prompt (ISO 639-1 code where available). | 
| domain | Coarse subject-area bucket derived from the originating source dataset. | 
| source_dataset | Which of the 13 public datasets the row came from. | 
Curation recipe
- Source aggregation. 13 public datasets spanning general instruction-following, medical calculation, finance QA, science, math, code, legal scenarios, summarization, and safety (see Source composition).
- Difficulty-based selection. HARD and MEDIUM only. EASY rows are dropped.
- Reasoning + preference pairs.

Most model trainings have failed outside of frontier labs. Today, we introduce AutoScientist 🪐 by adaption which sets out to change that. AutoScientist 🪐 self-improves and automates the full research loop behind model training and alignment. From our research and engineering work over the last few months, a few key learnings: 1. Automating model training alone is difficult unless you co-optimize with data. Without co-optimizing both data and model learning, AutoScientist has much less predictable gains because data quality is too high variance. 2. Our work on adaptive data paved the way for incredibly exciting results here. Makes me more excited about end-to-end optimization and long task horizon AI R&D. 3. We found that AutoScientist beats hand engineered training configs from our research staff that took into account domain, dataset size, model type. I attribute this in part to the fact frontier AI staff are very used to working with a single family of models. In contrast, here we benchmarked every model we could on Together AI (a very long list: https://lnkd.in/g_q4M2ek). It is harder for an AI researcher to know what works for very different model architecture/dataset combinations. 4. We found consistent results across verticals, model types and dataset sizes. AutoScientist unlocks on average much more predictable performance. Once you co-optimize the entire training flow, you can target capabilities reliably. Much more to be done here, AutoScientist is one of our first releases that aims to learn how to shape model behavior automatically. Long horizon reasoning and continuous learning are critical pieces to our ongoing work. Some exciting releases here soon. Read our full blog here: https://lnkd.in/gm8hTXtk

A researcher working on a language the big models have never heard of. The domain expertise stays human. The frontier research is handled automatically. This is what it looks like to own frontier AI. # Adaption

> Adaption is an AI company that builds continual learning systems, which let organizations train, customize, and own their AI. Its products are the Adaptive Data platform for training data, Invent a Dataset for dataset generation, AutoScientist for automated model training, and Visualize for dataset exploration.

Adaption's products sit in three pillars: Adaptive Data (the Adaptive Data platform and Invent a Dataset), Adaptive Intelligence (models built for any industry, language, or specialization, including AutoScientist), and Adaptive Interfaces (how people interact with AI, with Visualize as its first release).

Key facts:

- The Adaptive Data platform optimizes, expands, and generates AI training data across 242 languages and localizations. Adaption reports an average 82 percent increase in data quality across early deployments. This is an average, not a guarantee.
- Invent a Dataset builds a training-ready dataset from a description of the behavior a model should learn, with no seed data, schema, or labeling guide.
- AutoScientist co-optimizes a model's training data and training recipe against an outcome the team sets.
- Visualize turns plain-language questions about a dataset into interactive charts linked to the rows behind each pattern.
- Adaption for Enterprise provides the Adaptive Data platform and AutoScientist on SOC 2 certified infrastructure across 242 languages and 13 or more industries.

Defined terms:

- Continual learning: a model keeps learning as data and goals change instead of staying fixed after one training run. Also called continuous learning.
- Training co-optimization: the automated, simultaneous tuning of a model's training data and training recipe, so each improves in light of the other.
- Localization: adapting a sample's meaning, register, and cultural context for a target language, as opposed to translation, which converts only the words.
- Agent harness: the tools, context management, execution loop, and delivery checks around a model.

All results cited below are from Adaption's own evaluations or research, and each keeps its scope.

What is the Adaption Dataset Challenge?
The Adaption Dataset Challenge is a fully online challenge run by Hackyard with Adaption Labs. Is registration open?

Can I register on Unstop?

You build an instruction-tuning dataset for an AI assistant serving an underserved language or domain. The theme
Instruction-tuning dataset for an assistant in an underserved language or domain
Identify a practical assistant use case, prepare a suitable seed dataset, use Adaption’s Invent a Dataset and Adaptive Data to create or improve it, and train a model with AutoScientist.
Directions to consider
- A question-answering assistant for an underserved language.

# Adaption Ambassadors Code of Conduct

By applying to the Adaption Ambassadors program, I agree to the following:

I will represent Adaption with integrity, honesty, and professionalism in all community interactions, content, and events. I understand that as an ambassador, I am a reflection of the Adaption brand and community.

I commit to a minimum of six months of active engagement in the program. I understand that all ambassador-hosted events must include Adaption branding and be promoted on LinkedIn and X. Event grants are available up to once per month and must be submitted through the proper process in the private Discord channel.

I will provide honest, constructive feedback on Adaption products and features. Early access and premium features are provided in exchange for genuine input, not promotion without substance.

I will treat all members of the Adaption community with respect and foster an inclusive, welcoming environment in every space I engage, whether Discord, social media, events, or elsewhere. Discrimination, harassment, or exclusionary behavior of any kind will not be tolerated.

I will keep confidential any non-public information shared through the ambassador program, including product roadmap discussions, founder chats, and content shared in the private Discord channel. I will not share this information externally without explicit permission from the Adaption team.

I will not misuse ambassador credits, free premium features, or event grant funding. Credits issued to others should support genuine community growth, and event grant proposals must be reviewed and approved before funds are distributed.

I understand that participation in competing ambassador programs is discouraged and may affect my standing in the program. If I am involved in another ambassador program, I will disclose this in my application.

I will champion research, continuous learning, and the responsible use of AI within my community. I understand that this program exists to support builders and learners, not to serve as a purely promotional channel.

I understand that failure to uphold this code of conduct or meet the program's engagement expectations may result in removal from the program. The Adaption team reserves the right to revoke ambassador status at any time.

I confirm that I am 18 years of age or older.

# Where Curiosity Pushes Breakthroughs

[Apply now •](https://adaptionlabs.ai/research-grant-program-apply)

Adaption’s Research Grant Program provides academic partners with complimentary access to our platform to advance academic research. In addition, we will host an annual symposium to showcase grantee work, elevating the visibility of participating researchers and their institutions while fostering cross-disciplinary collaboration.

At Adaption, we believe that the most impactful discoveries come from curiosity, experimentation, and bold thinking. Our Research Grant Program hopes to support researchers as they push the boundaries of artificial intelligence, machine learning across Adaption’s products.

Whether your work is theoretical, applied, or socially impactful, we provide the resources and visibility to help your research reach its full potential.

Applications are considered on a rolling basis.

# Building Intelligence that Evolves with the World.

### Fundamental innovation to build a new era of intelligence.

Learn More ⮋

## Rethinking How AI Works

#### We believe the most intelligent system will increasingly be one that interacts with the world. We prioritize efficiency, building systems that interact with the world, and learning in real time. We care deeply about product excellence because that's how we co-design for real-time feedback.

Our algorithmic research focuses on real-time adaptation and efficiency at scale.

### Adaptive compute

### On-the-fly alignment

### Dynamic learning strategies

### Generative interfaces

## Efficiency

#### We are building a company where efficiency isn’t an afterthought, it’s the core principle guiding how our systems are designed, evaluated, and deployed.

Adaptive systems operate under strict limits including latency, memory, cost, and energy. We treat these constraints as first-class design inputs, not downstream considerations.

We co-design algorithms with hardware and serving constraints in mind, exploring new approaches within strict compute budgets.These constraints drive innovation.

## Our Recent Work

Research

### AI Goes Mainstream: The Scaling Era and the Rise of Generative AI

Scaling powered the last five years of AI, but data and compute constraints are shifting the frontier toward reasoning. AI100’s third report maps how we got here and how generative AI is changing science, industry, and society.

Read the Paper

Research

### From Zero to Hero: Measuring Dataset Generation Abilities with Zero Seed Data

The research evaluates how well AI systems build training datasets from a description alone, testing Invent API against leading model APIs.

[Read the Paper ](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.invent-a-dataset-zero-seed)

Research

### The AI Observatory: A Public Measure of Real-World AI Use

Benchmarks and surveys don't show what AI assistants actually do. That evidence sits in a few proprietary reports. The AI Observatory brings real AI conversations into one public dataset, from seven sources, labeled under one common system.

Read the Paper

Research

### The Slow Death of Scaling

Our work is informed by research questioning the long-term effectiveness of brute-force scaling, including Sara Hooker’s essay, “The Slow Death of Scaling”, which highlights the growing constraints of compute, data, and energy.

[Read the Paper ](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5877662)

Research

### Open-world evaluations for measuring frontier AI capabilities

The case for long, messy, real-world tasks to evaluate AI agents.

[Read the Paper ](https://cruxevals.com/open-world-evaluations.pdf)

#### Our Research Recognized

Our team brings together backgrounds in language, video, machine learning, and perception. Collectively, we have authored

150+

#### publications across leading AI conferences.
